nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.GodelII.tails_std
nodes.doc:
Walking along the tails of a premise list in `ℕ`, from the end: if the tails
`s₀, …, sₘ = 0` are coded by `(c', d')` and each `sⱼ` (`j < m`) is `⟨a, sⱼ₊₁⟩ + 1` with
`a` good, then every element of the list `sₘ₋ᵢ` is good.
nodes.type:
∀ {c' d' m : Nat} {Good : Nat → Prop},
  Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c' d' m 0 →
    (∀ (j : Nat),
        j < m →
          ∃ s,
            Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c' d' j s ∧
              ∃ t,
                Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c' d' (j + 1) t ∧
                  ∃ a, s = Foundations.Logic.Computability.pair a t + 1 ∧ Good a) →
      ∀ (i : Nat),
        i ≤ m →
          ∀ (s : Nat),
            Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c' d' (m - i) s →
              ∀ (z : Nat), z ∈ Foundations.Logic.Computability.decList s → Good z

    ∃ M e,

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.maschke
nodes.doc:
**Maschke's theorem.** Let `G` be a finite group and `K` a field in which `|G| ≠ 0`
(e.g. any field of characteristic zero). Then every subrepresentation `W` of a representation
`ρ` of `G` has an invariant complement `W'`: `K^ι = W ⊕ W'` as representations.
nodes.type:
∀ {K : Type w} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing K] {ι : Type v} [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType ι]
  {G : Type u} [inst_2 : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] [inst_3 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField K →
    Foundations.Algebra.ncast (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card G) ≠ 0 →
      ∀ (ρ : Foundations.Langlands.Rep G K ι) (W : Foundations.Langlands.Subspace ι K),
        Foundations.Langlands.Invariant ρ W → ∃ W', Foundations.Langlands.Invariant ρ W' ∧ W.IsCompl W'

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.Proves.witness
nodes.doc:
**The witness lemma** (Henkin). Suppose the variable `x` occurs free neither in
the premises `Δ` nor in `∃y φ(y)`. If `Δ ⊢ ∃y φ(y)` and `Δ ∪ {φ(x)}` is
inconsistent, then `Δ` itself is inconsistent. So a fresh variable can always be
consistently declared to be a witness.
nodes.type:
∀ {L : Foundations.Logic.FO.Signature} {Δ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Theory L} {φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula L}
  {x : Nat},
  (∀ (χ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula L), Δ χ → Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Fresh x χ) →
    Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Fresh x φ.ex →
      Δ ⊢₁ φ.ex →
        Δ.insert (φ.inst (Foundations.Logic.FO.Term.var x)) ⊢₁ Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.bot →
          Δ ⊢₁ Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.bot

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.GodelII.godel_second_of_dominates
nodes.doc:
**Gödel II for every predicate dominating `provH` at `⊥`.** Let `P` be any formula
such that `PA ⊢ provH(⌜⊥⌝) → P(⌜⊥⌝)` — "a `provH`-proof of `⊥` yields a `P`-proof of
`⊥`", provably in PA. Then PA does not prove `Con_P = ¬P(⌜⊥⌝)`. This is the single
PA-provable implication a textbook provability formula would have to satisfy in order to
inherit `godel_second_PA_unconditional`.
nodes.type:
∀ {P : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith},
  Foundations.Logic.FO.PA ⊢₁
      (Foundations.Logic.FO.box Foundations.Logic.FO.provH Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.bot).imp

      (fun d =>
        Foundations.NumberTheory.dchar χ d *
            Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal (Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt d / ↑d) *

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.gaussSum_twist
nodes.doc:
**The Gauss sum is an eigenvector of `ζ ↦ ζ^a`.** If `ζ^p = 1` and `p ∤ a`, replacing `ζ` by
`ζ^a` in the Gauss sum multiplies it by `(a/p)`:
`Σ_b (b/p) (ζ^a)^b = (a/p) · g`.
nodes.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing R] {p : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
    p % 2 = 1 →
      ∀ {ζ : R},
        ζ ^ p = 1 →
          ∀ {a : Nat},
            ¬p ∣ a →
              Foundations.Algebra.rsum (fun b => ↑(Foundations.Algebra.legendre b p) * (ζ ^ a) ^ b) p =
                ↑(Foundations.Algebra.legendre a p) * Foundations.Langlands.gaussSum p ζ

`log(m+1)/((m+1)m) ≤ g(m) − g(m+1)`. It reduces to `(m+1)(log(m+1) − log m) ≤ 2`, which follows
from `log y ≤ y − 1` at `y = (m+1)/m`.

  1 ≤ m →

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.iso_of_reindex
nodes.doc:
**Reindexing gives an isomorphic representation.** If `f : κ → ι` is a bijection (with

nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] {K : Type} [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing K] {ι κ : Type}
  [inst_2 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType ι] [inst_3 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType κ]
  (ρ : Foundations.Langlands.Rep G K ι) (σ : Foundations.Langlands.Rep G K κ) (f : κ → ι) (f' : ι → κ),
  (∀ (a : κ), f' (f a) = a) →
    (∀ (i : ι), f (f' i) = i) →
      (∀ (g : G) (a b : κ), σ.toFun g a b = ρ.toFun g (f a) (f b)) → Foundations.Langlands.Iso ρ σ

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.omega_nat_iso
nodes.doc:
**ω and Nat are isomorphic structures.** The map `Omega.toNat : ω → Nat` is a
bijection sending `∅` to `0`, set-successor to `+1`, `+ω` to `+`, `*ω` to `*`, and
inclusion to `≤`.
nodes.type:
Foundations.Sets.Bijective Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun ∧
  Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun Foundations.Bridges.Omega.zero = 0 ∧
    (∀ (x : Foundations.Bridges.Omega),
        Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun x.succ = Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun x + 1) ∧
      (∀ (x y : Foundations.Bridges.Omega),
          Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun (x.add y) =
            Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun x + Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun y) ∧
        (∀ (x y : Foundations.Bridges.Omega),
            Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun (x.mul y) =
              Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun x * Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun y) ∧
          ∀ (x y : Foundations.Bridges.Omega),
            x.le y ↔ Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun x ≤ Foundations.Bridges.omegaNat.toFun y

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.frobenius_sqrtField_tfae
nodes.doc:
**Three faces of one condition.** For distinct odd primes `p, q`, the following are
equivalent: (i) the Frobenius `σ_q` fixes `ℚ(√p*)` pointwise; (ii) `(q/p) = 1`, i.e. `q` is a
square modulo `p`; (iii) `p*` is a square modulo `q`. Condition (i) is the Galois-side form of
"`q` splits in `ℚ(√p*)`" (prime ideals are not formalised here); (i) ⇔ (ii) is Galois theory of
`ℚ(ζ_p)`, and (ii) ⇔ (iii) is quadratic reciprocity.
nodes.type:
∀ {p q : Nat} (hp : Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p) (hodd : p % 2 = 1),
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime q →
    q % 2 = 1 →
      p ≠ q →
        ∀ (hpq' : ¬p ∣ q),
          ((∀ (x : { x // x ∈ Foundations.Langlands.cycloField hp }),
                x.val ∈ Foundations.Langlands.sqrtField hp hodd → (Foundations.Langlands.galAut hp hpq').toFun x = x) ↔
              Foundations.Algebra.legendre q p = 1) ∧
            (Foundations.Algebra.legendre q p = 1 ↔ Foundations.Langlands.IsSqMod (Foundations.Langlands.pstar p) q)

nodes.name: Foundations.Geometry.Klein.not_euclid
nodes.doc:
**Euclid's axiom fails in the Klein model.** Take the angle at the origin between
the arms through `b = (1/2, 0)` and `c = (0, 1/2)`, and the point `t = (3/5, 3/5)` inside it
(beyond the midpoint `d` of `bc`). Any segment through `t` with endpoints on the two arms
would have endpoints `(σ, 0)`, `(0, ρ)` with `3/5 = (1−λ)σ` and `3/5 = λρ`; since
`σ, ρ < 1` inside the disc this gives `6/5 = (1−λ)σ + λρ < 1`, which is absurd. In
the Euclidean plane the endpoints would simply lie outside the unit circle.
nodes.type:
¬∀ (a b c d t : Foundations.Geometry.Klein.KPt),
    Foundations.Geometry.Klein.KBet a d t →
      Foundations.Geometry.Klein.KBet b d c →
        a ≠ d →
          ∃ x y,
            Foundations.Geometry.Klein.KBet a b x ∧
              Foundations.Geometry.Klein.KBet a c y ∧ Foundations.Geometry.Klein.KBet x t y

nodes.name: Foundations.Sets.ZFSet.hartogs_theorem
nodes.doc:
**Hartogs' theorem.** For every type `α` there is an ordinal `h` that does not
inject into `α`, and it is the least such: an ordinal `o` lies in `h` exactly when
`o` injects into `α`, and every ordinal not injecting into `α` contains or equals `h`.
(The construction makes no choices; see the module docstring for what
`#print axioms` reports.)
nodes.type:
∀ (α : Type),
  ∃ h,
    h.IsOrdinal ∧
      (¬∃ f, Function.Injective f) ∧
        (∀ (o : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), o.IsOrdinal → (o ∈ h ↔ ∃ f, Function.Injective f)) ∧
          ∀ (o : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), o.IsOrdinal → (¬∃ f, Function.Injective f) → h = o ∨ h ∈ o

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.frobenius_reciprocity_character
nodes.doc:
**Frobenius reciprocity for characters.** For a representation `σ` of `H` and a
representation `ρ` of `G`, `⟨Ind χ_σ, χ_ρ⟩_G = ⟨χ_σ, χ_{Res ρ}⟩_H`.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G] {ι κ : Type}
  [inst_2 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType ι] [inst_3 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType κ]
  (H : Foundations.Algebra.Subgroup G) (σ : Foundations.Langlands.Rep { x // x ∈ H } Foundations.Numbers.C ι)
  (ρ : Foundations.Langlands.Rep G Foundations.Numbers.C κ),
  Foundations.Langlands.natInv (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card G) *
      Foundations.Langlands.pairing (Foundations.Langlands.indFun H (Foundations.Langlands.character σ))
        (Foundations.Langlands.character ρ) =
    Foundations.Langlands.natInv (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card { x // x ∈ H }) *
      Foundations.Langlands.pairing (Foundations.Langlands.character σ)
        (Foundations.Langlands.character (Foundations.Langlands.Rep.res H ρ))

nodes.doc:
**A complete list of irreducibles exists.** Every finite group `G` has finitely many
pairwise non-isomorphic irreducible complex representations `ρ₀, …, ρ_{r−1}` such that every
irreducible complex representation of `G` (on an index type in `Type`) is isomorphic to one of
them.

      ∀ {κ : Type} [inst_2 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType κ]

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.hyperbola

**The hyperbola reindexing.** `Σ_{d ≤ N} Σ_{n ≤ N/d} g(d, n) = Σ_{m ≤ N} Σ_{d ∣ m} g(d, m/d)`
(all indices `≥ 1`): both sides run over the pairs `(d, n)` with `dn ≤ N`.
nodes.type:
∀ (N : Nat) (g : Nat → Nat → Foundations.Numbers.R),
  Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum
      (fun d => if 1 ≤ d then Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum (fun n => if 1 ≤ n then g d n else 0) (N / d + 1) else 0)
      (N + 1) =
    Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum
      (fun m => if 1 ≤ m then Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.dsum (fun d => g d (m / d)) m else 0) (N + 1)

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.selberg_local

**The local estimate.** For `1 ≤ d ≤ N`, with `Γ(d) = log(N/d) · Σ_{n ≤ N/d} Φ(dn)`:
`|Γ(d)| ≤ 4 log²(N/d) + 3`.
nodes.type:
∀ {γ : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  0 ≤ γ →
    γ ≤ 1 →
      (∀ (M : Nat),
          1 ≤ M →
            0 ≤ Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.harmonic M - (↑M).log - γ ∧
              ↑M * (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.harmonic M - (↑M).log - γ) ≤ 1) →
        ∀ {N d : Nat},
          1 ≤ d →
            d ≤ N →
              Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs
                  ((↑N / ↑d).log *
                    Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum
                      (fun n => if 1 ≤ n then Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.selbergPhi (γ + 1) N (d * n) else 0)
                      (N / d + 1)) ≤
                4 * ((↑N / ↑d).log * (↑N / ↑d).log) + 3

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.sum_sq_degrees
nodes.doc:
**Burnside's formula** `Σᵢ (dim ρᵢ)² = |G|`. If `ρ₀, …, ρ_{r−1}` are pairwise
non-isomorphic irreducible complex representations of a finite group `G`, and every irreducible
representation is isomorphic to one of them, then the squares of their degrees add up to `|G|`.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G] {r : Nat}
  {ιs : Fin r → Type} [inst_2 : (k : Fin r) → Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType (ιs k)]
  (ρs : (k : Fin r) → Foundations.Langlands.Rep G Foundations.Numbers.C (ιs k)),
  (∀ (k : Fin r), Foundations.Langlands.Irreducible (ρs k)) →
    (∀ (k k' : Fin r), k ≠ k' → ¬Foundations.Langlands.Iso (ρs k) (ρs k')) →
      (∀ {κ : Type} [inst_3 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType κ]
          (τ : Foundations.Langlands.Rep G Foundations.Numbers.C κ),
          Foundations.Langlands.Irreducible τ → ∃ k, Foundations.Langlands.Iso τ (ρs k)) →
        (Foundations.Langlands.natSum fun k =>
            Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card (ιs k) * Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card (ιs k)) =
          Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card G

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.factorization_unique
nodes.doc:
**Uniqueness of factorisation.** In an integral domain in which every irreducible element
is prime — for instance any principal ideal domain — two factorisations into irreducibles of
associated elements agree up to order and units: if `∏ L = u · ∏ M` with `u` a unit, then for
every `x`, `L` and `M` contain equally many factors associated to `x`.
nodes.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing R],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsDomain R →
    (∀ (p : R), Foundations.Algebra.Irreducible p → Foundations.Algebra.IsPrimeElt p) →
      ∀ (L M : List R) (u : R),
        (∀ (p : R), p ∈ L → Foundations.Algebra.Irreducible p) →
          (∀ (q : R), q ∈ M → Foundations.Algebra.Irreducible q) →
            Foundations.Algebra.IsUnit u →
              Foundations.Algebra.lprod L = u * Foundations.Algebra.lprod M →
                ∀ (x : R), Foundations.Algebra.countAssoc x L = Foundations.Algebra.countAssoc x M

at a time: removing a coset from such a set leaves such a set, with `|H|` fewer elements.

  (H : Foundations.Algebra.Subgroup G) (n : Nat) (P : G → Prop),
  Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.count P = n →
    (∀ (a h : G), P a → h ∈ H → P (a * h)) → (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.count fun x => x ∈ H) ∣ n

                          (∀ (x : N.Dom),

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.legendre_mul_gaussSum

            a < p →

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.root_primitive
nodes.doc:
**Roots of `P` are primitive.** If an irreducible rational polynomial `P` vanishes at `ζ_n`,
then each of its complex roots is a primitive `n`-th root of unity `ζ_n^j`,
`gcd(j, n) = 1`.
nodes.type:
∀ {n : Nat},
  1 ≤ n →
    ∀ {P : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial { x // x ∈ Foundations.Algebra.Qc }},
      Foundations.Algebra.Irreducible P →
        Foundations.Algebra.aeval Foundations.Algebra.Qc (Foundations.NumberTheory.zeta n) P = 0 →
          ∀ {«ω» : Foundations.Numbers.C},
            Foundations.Algebra.aeval Foundations.Algebra.Qc «ω» P = 0 →
              ∃ j, j < n ∧ j.Coprime n ∧ «ω» = Foundations.Algebra.rpow (Foundations.NumberTheory.zeta n) j

nodes.type:

  ∃ e,
    e ≠ 0 ∧
      Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Qp.std β v * Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Qp.std β' v' =
        e * e * Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Qp.std (β != β') (v * v')

∀ {n : Nat},

    ∀ («ω» : Foundations.Numbers.C),

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.chebyshev_bounds
nodes.doc:
**Chebyshev's bounds.** For every `m ≥ 6`,
`⌊m/2⌋ · log 2 ≤ π(m) · log m ≤ m · log 1024`.
So `π(m)` is of order `m / log m`: bounded above and below by constant multiples of it.
nodes.type:
∀ {m : Nat},
  6 ≤ m →
    ↑(m / 2) * Foundations.Numbers.R.log 2 ≤ ↑(Foundations.NumberTheory.primeCount m) * (↑m).log ∧
      ↑(Foundations.NumberTheory.primeCount m) * (↑m).log ≤ ↑m * Foundations.Numbers.R.log 1024

    w ∈ Foundations.Constructible.Def X →
      ∀ (a : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet),
        a ∈ X →
          ∃ φ ψ e,
            (∀ (n : Nat), e n ∈ X) ∧
              (∀ (y : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet),
                  y ∈ z ↔
                    y ∈ X ∧
                      Foundations.Constructible.RSat (fun x => x ∈ X) (Foundations.Forcing.BEnv.cons y e)
                        (Foundations.Constructible.evenF φ)) ∧
                ∀ (y : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet),
                  y ∈ w ↔
                    y ∈ X ∧
                      Foundations.Constructible.RSat (fun x => x ∈ X) (Foundations.Forcing.BEnv.cons y e)
                        (Foundations.Constructible.oddF ψ)

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.regular_multiplicity
nodes.doc:
**Multiplicity of an irreducible in the regular representation.** If the regular character
is `Σ_k m_k χ_k` for pairwise non-isomorphic irreducibles `ρ_k`, then `m_k = dim ρ_k`.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G] {r : Nat}
  {ιs : Fin r → Type} [inst_2 : (k : Fin r) → Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType (ιs k)]
  (ρs : (k : Fin r) → Foundations.Langlands.Rep G Foundations.Numbers.C (ιs k)),
  (∀ (k : Fin r), Foundations.Langlands.Irreducible (ρs k)) →
    (∀ (k k' : Fin r), k ≠ k' → ¬Foundations.Langlands.Iso (ρs k) (ρs k')) →
      ∀ (m : Fin r → Nat),
        (∀ (g : G),
            Foundations.Langlands.character (Foundations.Langlands.regularRep G Foundations.Numbers.C) g =
              Foundations.Algebra.isum fun k =>
                Foundations.Algebra.ncast (m k) * Foundations.Langlands.character (ρs k) g) →
          ∀ (j : Fin r), m j = Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card (ιs j)

nodes.name: Foundations.Combinatorics.hall
nodes.doc:
**Hall's marriage theorem.** Let `A₀, …, A_{N−1}` be subsets of `{0, …, M−1}` such
that every subfamily `I` has at least `|I|` elements in its union. Then there is a
system of distinct representatives: an injective choice `f(i) ∈ Aᵢ`.
nodes.type:
∀ (N M : Nat) (A : Nat → Nat → Prop),
  (∀ (I : Nat → Prop),
      Foundations.Combinatorics.cnt I N ≤ Foundations.Combinatorics.cnt (Foundations.Combinatorics.union N A I) M) →
    ∃ f, (∀ (i : Nat), i < N → f i < M ∧ A i (f i)) ∧ ∀ (i j : Nat), i < N → j < N → i ≠ j → f i ≠ f j

  Foundations.Geometry.Klein.n2 a < 1 →
    Foundations.Geometry.Klein.n2 b < 1 →

        a ≠ b →
          a.Bet b c →
            ∃ l m,
              0 ≤ l ∧
                0 < m ∧
                  ∀ (z : Foundations.Geometry.Pt Foundations.Numbers.R),
                    Foundations.Geometry.Klein.n2 z < 1 →

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Padic.min_le_vQ_add

  Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p →

      x ≠ 0 →
        y ≠ 0 →
          x + y ≠ 0 →
            min (Foundations.Langlands.Padic.vQ p x) (Foundations.Langlands.Padic.vQ p y) ≤
              Foundations.Langlands.Padic.vQ p (x + y)

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.aeval_zeta_pow_eq_zero
nodes.doc:
**Conjugates of `ζ_p`.** Every rational polynomial vanishing at `ζ_p` also vanishes at
`ζ_p^a` for `p ∤ a`.
nodes.type:
∀ {p : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
    ∀ {a : Nat},
      ¬p ∣ a →
        ∀ {f : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial { x // x ∈ Foundations.Algebra.Qc }},
          Foundations.Algebra.aeval Foundations.Algebra.Qc (Foundations.NumberTheory.zeta p) f = 0 →
            Foundations.Algebra.aeval Foundations.Algebra.Qc
                (Foundations.Algebra.rpow (Foundations.NumberTheory.zeta p) a) f =
              0

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.derived_fixes
nodes.doc:
**The derived series descends the tower.** For a Kummer chain `m = m₁ ++ m₂`, every element of
the `|m₂|`-th derived subgroup of `Aut(gen ℚ m / ℚ)` fixes the subfield `gen ℚ m₂`.
nodes.type:
∀ {m : List Foundations.Numbers.C},
  Foundations.Algebra.KummerChain m →
    ∀ (m₂ m₁ : List Foundations.Numbers.C),
      m = m₁ ++ m₂ →
        ∀ (σ : Foundations.Algebra.FieldAut Foundations.Algebra.Qc (Foundations.Algebra.gen Foundations.Algebra.Qc m)),
          σ ∈
              Foundations.Algebra.derivedSeries
                (Foundations.Algebra.FieldAut Foundations.Algebra.Qc (Foundations.Algebra.gen Foundations.Algebra.Qc m))
                m₂.length →
            σ.Fixes (Foundations.Algebra.gen Foundations.Algebra.Qc m₂)

  {A B : α → Prop}, S.M A → S.M B → (∀ (x : α), A x → B x → False) → (m.μ fun x => A x ∨ B x) = m.μ A + m.μ B

nodes.name: Foundations.Geometry.equilateral_of_sqrt3
nodes.doc:
Over any ordered field containing a square root of `3`, every segment `ab` is the side
of an equilateral triangle `abc`; for `a ≠ b` the apex `c` is off the line `ab`.
nodes.type:
∀ {K : Type} [inst : Lean.Grind.Field K] [inst_1 : LE K] [inst_2 : LT K] [inst_3 : Std.IsLinearOrder K]
  [Std.LawfulOrderLT K] [Lean.Grind.OrderedRing K] {r : K},
  r * r = 3 →
    ∀ (a b : Foundations.Geometry.Pt K),
      ∃ c, a.Cong b a c ∧ a.Cong b b c ∧ (a ≠ b → ¬a.Bet c b ∧ ¬c.Bet a b ∧ ¬a.Bet b c)

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.primeCount_two_mul_sub_unbounded
nodes.doc:
**More and more primes between `N` and `2N`.** `π(2N) − π(N)` is unbounded: for every `B`
there is `N` with more than `B` primes in `(N, 2N]`. Proof: eventually `π(2N)/π(N) > 3/2`
(`primeCount_two_mul_div_tendsto`), so `π(2N) − π(N) > π(N)/2`, and `π(N) → ∞`.
nodes.type: ∀ (B : Nat), ∃ N, B < Foundations.NumberTheory.primeCount (2 * N) - Foundations.NumberTheory.primeCount N

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.sat_PA_induction
nodes.doc: Meaning of an induction axiom.
nodes.type:
∀ {M : Foundations.Logic.FO.Structure Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith}
  (φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith) (e : Nat → M.Dom),
  Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat M e
      (((φ.inst Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith.zero).conj
            (φ.imp (Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.subst Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith.succSubst φ)).all).imp
        φ.all) ↔
    (Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat M (Foundations.Logic.FO.Env.cons (Foundations.Logic.FO.mz M) e) φ ∧
        ∀ (z : M.Dom),
          Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat M (Foundations.Logic.FO.Env.cons z e) φ →
            Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat M (Foundations.Logic.FO.Env.cons (Foundations.Logic.FO.ms M z) e) φ) →

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.sup_is_union
nodes.doc:
**Dedekind completeness, set-theoretically: the supremum is the union.** If `F` is
a nonempty set of reals (members of ℝ) bounded above by some real `M` (in the order
`⊆`), then the union `⋃F` is again a real, it is an upper bound of `F`, and it lies
below every upper bound. The proof uses nothing but the definition of a cut.

∀ {F M : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet},
  F ⊆ Foundations.Bridges.RSet →
    (∃ A, A ∈ F) →
      M ∈ Foundations.Bridges.RSet →
        (∀ (A : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), A ∈ F → A ⊆ M) →
          ⋃₀ F ∈ Foundations.Bridges.RSet ∧
            (∀ (A : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), A ∈ F → A ⊆ ⋃₀ F) ∧
              ∀ (M' : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), (∀ (A : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), A ∈ F → A ⊆ M') → ⋃₀ F ⊆ M'

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial.div_mod_aux
nodes.doc:
**Division with remainder by a polynomial with invertible leading coefficient.** If `g`
has degree `≤ m` and its coefficient at `m` is a unit (with inverse `u`), then every `p` can
be written `p = q * g + r` with `deg r < m`. Proved by long division: cancel the top
coefficient of `p` with a multiple `c u X^(k-m) g`, and recurse.
nodes.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing R] (g : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial R) (m : Nat) (u : R),
  g.DegLT (m + 1) →
    g.coeff m * u = 1 → ∀ (d : Nat) (p : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial R), p.DegLT d → ∃ q r, p = q * g + r ∧ r.DegLT m

    (∀ (x : α), 0 ≤ g x) →
      ∀ {φ ψ : List (Foundations.Numbers.R × (α → Prop))},
        Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.IsSimple S φ →
          Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.IsSimple S ψ →
            Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Below φ f →
              Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Below ψ g →
                (Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.BddIntegral m fun x => f x + g x) →

                Foundations.Logic.FO.fcode (Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.subst σ φ) =

                      (Foundations.Logic.FO.fcode (Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.subst σ A))
                      (Foundations.Logic.FO.fcode (Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.subst σ B)))) →
              ∀ (dp r : Foundations.Logic.FO.stdPA.Dom),
                Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.Entry tc td L (Foundations.Logic.FO.fcode φ) dp r 1 →
                  (∀ (dp r : Foundations.Logic.FO.stdPA.Dom),
                      Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.Entry tc td L (Foundations.Logic.FO.fcode A) dp r 1 →
                        r =
                          Foundations.Logic.FO.fcode
                            (Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.subst

nodes.name: Foundations.Forcing.decide_countable
nodes.doc:
**Deciding lemma (σ-closed forcing adds no new countable sequences).** Let `K` be
countable and, for each `k : K`, let `V k : J → Col I` be a family of possible answers with
`c ≤ ⨆_j V k j`. Then below every condition `p ∈ c` there is a single condition `r` and an
answer `ζ k` for every question `k` with `r ∈ V k (ζ k)` for all `k`. The conditions are found
one question at a time and the resulting descending sequence has a lower bound.
nodes.type:
∀ {I K J : Type},
  Foundations.Sets.Countable K →
    ∀ (c : Foundations.Forcing.Col I) (V : K → J → Foundations.Forcing.Col I),
      (∀ (k : K), c ≤ Foundations.Forcing.CBA.iSup (V k)) →
        ∀ {p : Foundations.Forcing.CCond I}, c.carrier p → ∃ r, r ≤ p ∧ ∃ ζ, ∀ (k : K), (V k (ζ k)).carrier r

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.galois_correspondence
nodes.doc:
**Galois correspondence (the part formalised here).** For a Galois extension `L/K` with
Galois group enumerated as `σ₁, …, σₙ`:
* `[L : Fix(G)] = |G| = [L : K]` and `Fix(G) = K`;
* for every finite subgroup `H` (given as a family `ρ`), `[L : Fix(H)] = |H|` and
  `Aut(L/Fix(H)) = H`.
nodes.type:
∀ {Ω : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing Ω],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField Ω →
    ∀ {K L : Foundations.Algebra.Subfield Ω} (hKL : K.le L),
      Foundations.Algebra.IsGalois K L hKL →
        (∀ (x : Ω), (x ∈ Foundations.Algebra.fixedField L fun x => True) → x ∈ K) ∧
          ∀ {m : Nat} (ρ : Fin m → Foundations.Algebra.FieldAut K L),
            (∀ (i j : Fin m), ρ i = ρ j → i = j) →
              (∃ i, ρ i = 1) →
                (∀ (i j : Fin m), ∃ k, ρ k = ρ i * ρ j) →
                  (Foundations.Algebra.famFix ρ).deg L ⋯ = m ∧
                    ∀ (τ : Foundations.Algebra.FieldAut (Foundations.Algebra.famFix ρ) L), ∃ i, (ρ i).toFun = τ.toFun

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.rat_in_sets
nodes.doc:
**The rationals live in the set-theoretic universe.** The comparison map from
Part II's rationals `Q` to the ZF set `ℚ` (classes of pairs `⟪x, k⟫` with `x` in the
ZF set `ℤ` and `k ∈ ω ∖ {∅}`) is a bijection onto the members of `ℚ` preserving
`0`, `1`, addition, negation, multiplication and order.
nodes.type:
(Foundations.Sets.Bijective fun x => ⟨Foundations.Bridges.qToSet x, ⋯⟩) ∧
  Foundations.Bridges.qToSet 0 = Foundations.Bridges.qzero ∧
    Foundations.Bridges.qToSet 1 = Foundations.Bridges.qone ∧
      (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Q),
          Foundations.Bridges.qToSet (x + y) =
            Foundations.Bridges.qadd (Foundations.Bridges.qToSet x) (Foundations.Bridges.qToSet y)) ∧
        (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.Q),
            Foundations.Bridges.qToSet (-x) = Foundations.Bridges.qneg (Foundations.Bridges.qToSet x)) ∧
          (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Q),
              Foundations.Bridges.qToSet (x * y) =
                Foundations.Bridges.qmul (Foundations.Bridges.qToSet x) (Foundations.Bridges.qToSet y)) ∧
            ∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Q),
              x ≤ y ↔ Foundations.Bridges.qle (Foundations.Bridges.qToSet x) (Foundations.Bridges.qToSet y)

nodes.name: Foundations.Probability.FinProb.weak_law_limit
nodes.doc:
**The weak law of large numbers, limit form**: for every `ε > 0` and `δ > 0` there is
`N` such that for all `n ≥ N`, `Pⁿ(|Sₙ/n − μ| ≥ ε) ≤ δ` — the sample mean converges to
the true mean in probability.
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} (P : Foundations.Probability.FinProb α) (X : α → Foundations.Numbers.R) {ε δ : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  0 < ε →
    0 < δ →
      ∃ N,
        ∀ (n : Nat),
          N ≤ n →
            0 < n →
              ((P.pow n).prob fun t =>
                  ε ≤ Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (Foundations.Probability.FinProb.sampleSum X n t / ↑n - P.E X)) ≤
                δ

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.gsum_exp_mul
nodes.doc:
**Cauchy product of exponential series**, finite form:
`Pₙ(a) Pₙ(b) = Pₙ(a + b) + Tₙ(a, b)` with `Pₙ(x) = Σ_{k<n} e x k`.
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} [inst : Lean.Grind.Field α] (e : α → Nat → α),
  (∀ (x : α), e x 0 = 1) →
    (∀ (x : α) (n : Nat), (↑n + 1) * e x (n + 1) = x * e x n) →
      (∀ (n : Nat), ↑n + 1 ≠ 0) →
        ∀ (a b : α) (N : Nat),
          Foundations.Numbers.gsum (e a) N * Foundations.Numbers.gsum (e b) N =
            Foundations.Numbers.gsum (e (a + b)) N +
              Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun i => e a i * Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun k => e b (N - i + k)) i) N

with `F(∅) = a` and `F(succ n) = G(F(n))`.

              ∀ (F' : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet),
                F'.IsFunction ω A →

    (∀ (φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith),
        Foundations.Logic.FO.PA ⊢₁

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.iso_dsum_of_compl
nodes.doc:

non-zero, then `ρ ≅ ρ₁ ⊕ ρ₂` for representations `ρ₁`, `ρ₂` of degrees `d, e ≥ 1` with

∀ {K : Type w} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing K] {G : Type u} [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.Group G],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField K →

      {W W' : Foundations.Langlands.Subspace ι K},
      Foundations.Langlands.Invariant ρ W →
        Foundations.Langlands.Invariant ρ W' →
          W.IsCompl W' →
            ¬W.IsZero →
              ¬W'.IsZero →
                ∃ d e,
                  0 < d ∧
                    0 < e ∧
                      d + e ≤ Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card ι ∧ ∃ ρ₁ ρ₂, Foundations.Langlands.Iso ρ (ρ₁.dsum ρ₂)

  1 ≤ m →

      (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.psi n - Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.psi m) * (↑m).log ≤

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Padic.not_ordered
nodes.doc:
**ℤₚ is not ordered like ℝ (odd `p`).** For an odd prime `p`, there is no relation `≤` on
`ℤₚ` that is preserved by adding a constant, makes every square non-negative, and has `¬ 1 ≤ 0`.
(Every ordered ring has these properties; the obstruction is that `1 − p` is a square in ℤₚ.)
nodes.type:
∀ {p : Nat},
  Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p →
    p % 2 = 1 →
      ∀ (le : Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp p → Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp p → Prop),
        (∀ (a b c : Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp p), le a b → le b c → le a c) →
          (∀ (a b c : Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp p), le a b → le (a + c) (b + c)) →
            (∀ (x : Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp p), le 0 (x * x)) → ¬le 1 0 → False

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Gentzen.consistency_by_descent
nodes.doc:
**Consistency by ordinal descent** (the abstract form of Gentzen's argument).
Let `D` be a type of objects (e.g. derivations), `Bad` a property of them (e.g. "is
a derivation of the empty sequent"), and `o` an assignment of ordinal notations
below ε₀ in Cantor normal form. If every bad object can be reduced to a bad object of
strictly smaller ordinal, then no object is bad. The proof is transfinite induction
up to ε₀, i.e. the well-foundedness theorem `wellFounded_R`.
nodes.type:
∀ {D : Type} (Bad : D → Prop) (o : D → Foundations.Logic.Ordinals.ON),
  (∀ (d : D), (o d).NF) → (∀ (d : D), Bad d → ∃ d', Bad d' ∧ (o d').lt (o d)) → ∀ (d : D), ¬Bad d

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Sequent.derives_iff_cutFree
nodes.doc:

from a (possibly infinite) theory `Γ` iff some finite list `L` of premises from `Γ`

(distinct, containing the identity, closed under composition), then any `m > n` elements of `L`
are linearly dependent over `Fix(H)`.

∀ {Ω : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing Ω] {K L : Foundations.Algebra.Subfield Ω} {n : Nat}
  (σ : Fin n → Foundations.Algebra.FieldAut K L),
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField Ω →
    (∀ (i j : Fin n), σ i = σ j → i = j) →
      (∃ i, σ i = 1) →
        (∀ (i j : Fin n), ∃ k, σ k = σ i * σ j) →
          ∀ {m : Nat} (a : Fin m → { x // x ∈ L }),
            n < m →
              ∃ c,
                (∃ j, c j ≠ 0) ∧
                  (∀ (j : Fin m), (c j).val ∈ Foundations.Algebra.famFix σ) ∧
                    (Foundations.Algebra.isum fun j => c j * a j) = 0

nodes.name: Foundations.Sets.Zorn.zorn
nodes.doc:

antisymmetric). If every chain has an upper bound, then there is a maximal
element: some `m` such that `r m x` implies `x = m`.
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type u} {r : α → α → Prop},
  (∀ (x : α), r x x) →
    (∀ (x y z : α), r x y → r y z → r x z) →
      (∀ (x y : α), r x y → r y x → x = y) →
        (∀ (c : α → Prop), Foundations.Sets.Zorn.IsChain r c → ∃ u, ∀ (x : α), c x → r x u) →
          ∃ m, ∀ (x : α), r m x → x = m

nodes.name: Foundations.Probability.FinProb.weak_law
nodes.doc:
**The weak law of large numbers** (Bernoulli 1713, in Chebyshev's form). For `n ≥ 1`
independent repetitions and any `ε > 0`,

`Pⁿ(|Sₙ/n − μ| ≥ ε) ≤ σ² / (n ε²)`, where `μ = E[X]`, `σ² = Var X`.
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} (P : Foundations.Probability.FinProb α) (X : α → Foundations.Numbers.R) {n : Nat},
  0 < n →
    ∀ {ε : Foundations.Numbers.R},
      0 < ε →
        ((P.pow n).prob fun t =>
            ε ≤ Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (Foundations.Probability.FinProb.sampleSum X n t / ↑n - P.E X)) ≤
          P.Var X / (↑n * (ε * ε))

nodes.name: Foundations.Forcing.BSet.le_isFunc_inf_isInj
nodes.doc:
**Criterion for an injective function.** The graph name `F = fname s t w` is, to degree
`c`, an injective function from `X` to `Y`, provided that (to degree `c`) every member of `X`
is some listed `sⱼ` with weight `wⱼ` and `tⱼ ∈ Y`; listed pairs with equal first coordinates
have equal second coordinates; and listed pairs with equal second coordinates have equal first
coordinates.
nodes.type:
∀ {B : Type} [inst : Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra B] {J : Type} {s t : J → Foundations.Forcing.BSet B}
  {w : J → B} {X Y : Foundations.Forcing.BSet B} {c : B},
  (∀ (u : Foundations.Forcing.BSet B),
      Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.inf c (u.mem X) ≤
        Foundations.Forcing.CBA.iSup fun j =>
          Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.inf
            (Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.inf (w j) (u.eq (s j))) ((t j).mem Y)) →
    (∀ (j j' : J),
        Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.inf
            (Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.inf (Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.inf c (w j))
              (w j'))
            ((s j).eq (s j')) ≤
          (t j).eq (t j')) →
      (∀ (j j' : J),
          Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.inf
              (Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.inf (Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.inf c (w j))
                (w j'))
              ((t j).eq (t j')) ≤
            (s j).eq (s j')) →
        c ≤
          Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.inf ((Foundations.Forcing.BSet.fname s t w).isFunc X Y)
            ((Foundations.Forcing.BSet.fname s t w).isInj X)

          Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Legendre.Nontriv x' y' z' ∧
            Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Legendre.Primitive x' y' z' ∧ a * (x' * x') + b * (y' * y') + c * (z' * z') = 0

nodes.doc:

                  q * (x + 1) / p

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.godel_second_PA_unconditional
nodes.doc:
**Gödel's second incompleteness theorem for PA.** Unconditionally, PA does not prove
the consistency statement `¬provH(⌜⊥⌝)` for the provability formula `provH`, which defines
PA-provability in the standard model and satisfies (D1)–(D3) provably in PA.

Caveat (Gödel II is intensional, Feferman 1960): `provH` is not the textbook "there is a
PA-derivation of x"; its proofs are modus-ponens/necessitation closures of a Σ₁ listing of
PA's theorems, and PA-provable equivalence of `conF provH` with the canonical Con(PA) is not
established here. `provH` contains no consistency filter, so this is a genuine instance of
the Hilbert–Bernays–Löb form of the theorem, not a Feferman-style artefact (contrast
`GodelII.provF`, which has the same extension in `ℕ` but fails (D2) and has a PA-provable
consistency statement). For the derivation-based formula `provD`, Gödel II is reduced to
(D3) in `GodelII.godel_second_provD_of_D3`, and to `PA ⊢ provH(⌜⊥⌝) → provD(⌜⊥⌝)` in
`GodelII.godel_second_provD_of_dominates`; neither hypothesis is proved. For the derivation
predicate `provDP`, Gödel II is proved without hypotheses (`godel_second_provDP`).
nodes.type: ¬Foundations.Logic.FO.PA ⊢₁ Foundations.Logic.FO.conF Foundations.Logic.FO.provH

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Padic.hensel_strong
nodes.doc:
**Hensel's lemma, strong form.** Let `p` be prime, `f` an integer polynomial and `a` an
integer with `vₚ(f'(a)) = e` (i.e. `pᵉ ∣ f'(a)`, `pᵉ⁺¹ ∤ f'(a)`) and `p^(2e+1) ∣ f(a)` — that is,
`|f(a)|ₚ < |f'(a)|ₚ²`. Then there is `x ∈ ℤₚ` with `f(x) = 0` and `x ≡ a (mod pᵉ⁺¹)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {p : Nat},
  Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p →
    ∀ (f : List Int) (a : Int) (e : Nat),
      ↑p ^ e ∣ Foundations.Langlands.Padic.pderiv f a →
        ¬↑p ^ (e + 1) ∣ Foundations.Langlands.Padic.pderiv f a →
          ↑p ^ (2 * e + 1) ∣ Foundations.Langlands.Padic.peval f a →
            ∃ x, Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp.peval f x = 0 ∧ Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp.ModPow (e + 1) x ↑a

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Squares.legendre_eq_char
nodes.doc:
**Multiplicativity in the top argument, against a character.** Let `q` be an odd prime and
`χ` a function on odd numbers with `χ(1) = 1` and `χ(ab) = χ(a)χ(b)`. If `(p/q) = χ(p)` for every
prime factor `p` of the odd number `m`, then `(m/q) = χ(m)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {q : Nat},
  Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime q →
    q % 2 = 1 →
      ∀ (χ : Nat → Int),
        χ 1 = 1 →
          (∀ (a b : Nat), a % 2 = 1 → b % 2 = 1 → χ (a * b) = χ a * χ b) →
            ∀ (m : Nat),
              m % 2 = 1 →
                (∀ (p : Nat), Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p → p ∣ m → Foundations.Algebra.legendre p q = χ p) →
                  Foundations.Algebra.legendre m q = χ m

    Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.count R * Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.count fun x => x ∈ H

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.eisenstein_conv
nodes.doc:
**Eisenstein's criterion over `ℤ`.** Let `F` be the coefficient sequence of a monic integer
polynomial of degree `n`, and `p` a prime dividing `F₀, …, F_{n-1}` with `p² ∤ F₀`. Then `F` is
not a product of integer polynomials of degrees `d` and `n - d` with `1 ≤ d < n`.
nodes.type:
∀ {p : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
    ∀ {F : Nat → Int} {n : Nat},
      F n = 1 →
        (∀ (k : Nat), k < n → ↑p ∣ F k) →
          ¬↑p * ↑p ∣ F 0 →
            ∀ {G H : Nat → Int} {d : Nat},
              1 ≤ d →
                d < n →
                  (∀ (m : Nat), F m = Foundations.Algebra.conv G H m) →
                    Foundations.Algebra.SuppLE G d → Foundations.Algebra.SuppLE H (n - d) → False

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.secondIsoTheorem
nodes.doc:
**Second isomorphism theorem** (the "diamond" isomorphism). For a subgroup `H` and a
normal subgroup `N` of `G`, `H ⧸ (H ∩ N) ≃* HN ⧸ N`. Here `H ∩ N` and `N` are viewed as
(normal) subgroups of `H` and of `HN` respectively, via preimages under the inclusions.
nodes.type:
{G : Type u} →
  [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] →
    (H N : Foundations.Algebra.Subgroup G) →
      [hN : N.Normal] →
        Foundations.Algebra.Iso
          (Foundations.Algebra.QuotientGroup (Foundations.Algebra.Subgroup.comap (Foundations.Algebra.Hom.subtype H) N))
          (Foundations.Algebra.QuotientGroup
            (Foundations.Algebra.Subgroup.comap (Foundations.Algebra.Hom.subtype (H.prodNormal N)) N))

nodes.name: Foundations.Geometry.rat_plane_axioms
nodes.doc:
**The rational plane satisfies the field-independent Tarski axioms**: (A1)–(A3),
(A5)–(A10) hold in `ℚ²` (they hold over every ordered field). Together with the two
failures above, this locates exactly where the real numbers are needed.
nodes.type:
(∀ (a b : Foundations.Geometry.Pt Foundations.Numbers.Q), a.Cong b b a) ∧
  (∀ (a b c : Foundations.Geometry.Pt Foundations.Numbers.Q), a.Cong b c c → a = b) ∧
    (∀ (a b : Foundations.Geometry.Pt Foundations.Numbers.Q), a.Bet b a → a = b) ∧
      (∀ (a b c p q : Foundations.Geometry.Pt Foundations.Numbers.Q),
          a.Bet p c → b.Bet q c → ∃ x, p.Bet x b ∧ q.Bet x a) ∧
        (∃ a b c, ¬a.Bet b c ∧ ¬b.Bet c a ∧ ¬c.Bet a b) ∧
          ∀ (a b c d t : Foundations.Geometry.Pt Foundations.Numbers.Q),
            a.Bet d t → b.Bet d c → a ≠ d → ∃ x y, a.Bet b x ∧ a.Bet c y ∧ x.Bet t y

nodes.name: Foundations.Probability.FinProb.bayes_partition
nodes.doc: **Bayes' theorem for a partition**: `P(Bⱼ | A) = P(A | Bⱼ) P(Bⱼ) / ∑ᵢ P(A | Bᵢ) P(Bᵢ)`.

          P.cond (B j) A =

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.R.rolle

**Rolle's theorem.** If `f` is continuous at every point of `[a, b]`, differentiable on `(a, b)`, and

nodes.type:
∀ {f f' : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R} {a b : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  a < b →
    (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), a ≤ x → x ≤ b → Foundations.Numbers.R.ContinuousAt f x) →
      (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), a < x → x < b → Foundations.Numbers.R.HasDerivAt f (f' x) x) →
        f a = f b → ∃ c, a < c ∧ c < b ∧ f' c = 0

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.good_weight
nodes.doc:
**The combinatorial core of the improvement.** Suppose `|V(n)| ≤ α` for `n ≥ N₀`, and
`m_j` (`j = 0, 1, …`) are left ends of good intervals (`|V| ≤ ε/2` on `[m_j, m_j + ⌊m_j/T⌋]`),
increasing fast enough (`m_{j+1} ≥ m_j + ⌊m_j/T⌋`), with `m_j ≥ Y₀ ≥ N₀`, `m_j ≥ 2T`, and
`64 T² m_j² ≤ N` for `j < J`. Then, with `S = Σ_{k ≤ N} (a(k)/k) |V(⌊N/k⌋)|`,
`8T (α F(N) + C₀ (F(N) − F(N/Y₀)) − S) ≥ J (α − ε/2)(log N − 16 T KA)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {ε α : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  ε ≤ α →
    0 < ε →
      ∀ {N₀ Y₀ T N J : Nat},
        1 ≤ T →
          N₀ ≤ Y₀ →
            1 ≤ Y₀ →
              (∀ (n : Nat), N₀ ≤ n → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vrem n) ≤ α) →
                ∀ (m : Nat → Nat),
                  (∀ (j : Nat), Y₀ ≤ m j) →
                    (∀ (j : Nat), 2 * T ≤ m j) →
                      (∀ (j : Nat), m j + m j / T ≤ m (j + 1)) →
                        (∀ (j n : Nat),
                            m j ≤ n →
                              n ≤ m j + m j / T →
                                Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vrem n) ≤ ε / 2) →
                          (∀ (j : Nat), j < J → 64 * (T * T) * (m j * m j) ≤ N) →
                            ↑J * ((α - ε / 2) * ((↑N).log - 16 * ↑T * Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.KA)) ≤
                              8 * ↑T *
                                (α * Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.wsum N +
                                    Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.C0 *
                                      (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.wsum N -
                                        Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.wsum (N / Y₀)) -
                                  Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum
                                    (fun k =>
                                      Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.selA k * (1 / ↑k) *
                                        Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vrem (N / k)))
                                    (N + 1))

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.Q.ordered_field
nodes.doc:
**`Q` is an ordered field (summary).** The field laws hold, and `≤` is a linear order
compatible with addition and with multiplication by positive elements.
nodes.type:
(∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.Q), x + y + z = x + (y + z)) ∧
  (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Q), x + y = y + x) ∧
    (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.Q), x + 0 = x) ∧
      (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.Q), -x + x = 0) ∧
        (∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.Q), x * y * z = x * (y * z)) ∧
          (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Q), x * y = y * x) ∧
            (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.Q), x * 1 = x) ∧
              (∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.Q), x * (y + z) = x * y + x * z) ∧
                0 ≠ 1 ∧
                  (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.Q), x ≠ 0 → x * x⁻¹ = 1) ∧
                    (∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.Q), x ≤ y → y ≤ z → x ≤ z) ∧
                      (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Q), x ≤ y → y ≤ x → x = y) ∧
                        (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Q), x ≤ y ∨ y ≤ x) ∧
                          (∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.Q), x ≤ y → x + z ≤ y + z) ∧
                            ∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.Q), x < y → 0 < z → z * x < z * y

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.frobenius_gaussSum_general
nodes.doc:
**Frobenius acts on the Gauss sum as the residue `q`.** In a commutative ring of
characteristic `q` containing a `p`-th root of unity `ζ`, the Gauss sum satisfies
`g^q = (q/p) · g`: the `q`-th power map sends `ζ^a` to `ζ^{qa}` and the substitution
`a ↦ qa` multiplies the Legendre symbol by `(q/p)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing R] {p q : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
    p % 2 = 1 →
      Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime q →
        q % 2 = 1 →
          p ≠ q →
            ∀ {ζ : R},
              ζ ^ p = 1 →
                ↑↑q = 0 →
                  Foundations.Langlands.gaussSum p ζ ^ q =
                    ↑(Foundations.Algebra.legendre q p) * Foundations.Langlands.gaussSum p ζ

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.godel_first_incompleteness

proved relative to Lean in `PeanoArithmetic`). There is a *sentence* `σ` of arithmetic
(no free variables) which is true in the standard model `ℕ`, yet PA proves neither
`σ` nor its negation `¬σ`.
nodes.type:
∃ σ,
  Foundations.Logic.FO.IsSentence σ ∧
    (∀ (e : Nat → Nat), Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat Foundations.Logic.FO.stdModel e σ) ∧
      ¬Foundations.Logic.FO.PA ⊢₁ σ ∧ ¬Foundations.Logic.FO.PA ⊢₁ σ.neg

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.uniform_square
nodes.doc:
**Uniform continuity on the square.** (A Lebesgue-number lemma for `[0, 1]²`.) For jointly
continuous `H` and `ε > 0` there is `δ > 0` such that `H(s, u)` and `H(s, v)` are `ε`-close
whenever `s, u, v ∈ [0, 1]` and `|u − v| < δ`.
nodes.type:
∀ {X : Type} [inst : Foundations.Topology.MetricSpace X] {H : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R → X},
  Foundations.Topology.Cont2 H →
    ∀ {ε : Foundations.Numbers.R},
      0 < ε →
        ∃ δ,
          0 < δ ∧
            ∀ (s u v : Foundations.Numbers.R),
              0 ≤ s →
                s ≤ 1 →
                  0 ≤ u →
                    u ≤ 1 →
                      0 ≤ v →
                        v ≤ 1 → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (u - v) < δ → Foundations.Topology.dist (H s u) (H s v) < ε

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.degree_homotopy
nodes.doc:
**Homotopy invariance of the degree.** If `H(s, ·)` is a loop in the circle for every
`s ∈ [0, 1]` (a *free* homotopy: the base point `H(s, 0)` may move), then `H(0, ·)` and `H(1, ·)`
have the same degree.
nodes.type:
∀ {H : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.C},
  Foundations.Topology.Cont2 H →
    (∀ (s t : Foundations.Numbers.R), 0 ≤ s → s ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → (H s t).normSq = 1) →
      (∀ (s : Foundations.Numbers.R), 0 ≤ s → s ≤ 1 → H s 1 = H s 0) →
        Foundations.Topology.degree (H 0) = Foundations.Topology.degree (H 1)

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.GodelII.provD_no_contradiction

∀ (N : Nat),
  Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum

nodes.name: Foundations.Forcing.RO.ccc_of_poset
nodes.doc:
**ccc transfers from a poset to its regular-open algebra.** If every antichain of
conditions is countable, then every family of non-zero, pairwise disjoint regular open sets
is countable. Pick a condition in each set: distinct sets give incompatible conditions.
nodes.type:
∀ {P : Type} [inst : Foundations.Forcing.ForcingNotion P],
  (∀ (A : P → Prop), Foundations.Forcing.ForcingNotion.IsAntichain A → Foundations.Sets.Countable { p // A p }) →
    ∀ (S : Foundations.Forcing.RO P → Prop),
      (∀ (U : Foundations.Forcing.RO P), S U → U ≠ Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.bot) →
        (∀ (U V : Foundations.Forcing.RO P),
            S U →
              S V →
                U ≠ V →
                  Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.inf U V = Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.bot) →
          Foundations.Sets.Countable { U // S U }

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.int_in_sets
nodes.doc:
**The integers live in the set-theoretic universe.** The comparison map from
Part II's integers `Z` to the ZF set `ℤ` of equivalence classes of pairs in `ω × ω`
is a bijection onto the members of `ℤ` that preserves `0`, `1`, addition, negation,
multiplication and order — all of which are defined on the set side by the ZF
axioms alone (pairs, products, separation, power set, and `+ω`, `*ω`).
nodes.type:
(Foundations.Sets.Bijective fun x => ⟨Foundations.Bridges.zToSet x, ⋯⟩) ∧
  Foundations.Bridges.zToSet 0 = Foundations.Bridges.zzero ∧
    Foundations.Bridges.zToSet 1 = Foundations.Bridges.zone ∧
      (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
          Foundations.Bridges.zToSet (x + y) =
            Foundations.Bridges.zadd (Foundations.Bridges.zToSet x) (Foundations.Bridges.zToSet y)) ∧
        (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
            Foundations.Bridges.zToSet (-x) = Foundations.Bridges.zneg (Foundations.Bridges.zToSet x)) ∧
          (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
              Foundations.Bridges.zToSet (x * y) =
                Foundations.Bridges.zmul (Foundations.Bridges.zToSet x) (Foundations.Bridges.zToSet y)) ∧
            ∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
              x ≤ y ↔ Foundations.Bridges.zle (Foundations.Bridges.zToSet x) (Foundations.Bridges.zToSet y)

nodes.doc:
**Banach's fixed-point theorem.** On a complete metric space, a contraction `f`
(`d(f x, f y) ≤ q d(x, y)` with `0 ≤ q < 1`) has a unique fixed point, and the orbit of every

            ∀ (x₀ : X),

                  Foundations.Topology.Converges (Foundations.Topology.orbit f x₀) x ∧ ∀ (y : X), f y = y → y = x

nodes.name: Foundations.Categories.Adjunction.preservesLimit

a cone `W ⟶ G (K j)` across the adjunction to a cone `F W ⟶ K j`, factors that through
`c`, and transposes back.

{J : Type u₁} →

            {F : Foundations.Categories.Functor C D} →

                Foundations.Categories.Adjunction F G →

        Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Legendre.Primitive x y z →

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.prime_dvd_sum_le
nodes.doc:
**Primes dividing `q` contribute boundedly.**
`Σ_{p ≤ N} Σ_{k ≤ N} [p prime, p ∣ q, k ≥ 1, pᵏ ≤ N] log p / pᵏ ≤ 2q` for `q ≥ 1`.

∀ {q : Nat},
  0 < q →
    ∀ (N : Nat),
      Foundations.Numbers.gsum

                if (Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p ∧ 1 ≤ k ∧ p ^ k ≤ N) ∧ p ∣ q then

                else 0)
              (N + 1))

        2 * ↑q

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Legendre.isSqMod_of_Qp
nodes.doc:
**The local condition at an odd prime `p ∣ a`.** If `a` is squarefree, `p ∤ bc`, and
`a x² + b y² + c z² = 0` has a non-trivial point in ℚₚ, then `−bc` is a square modulo `p`.
Writing `a = p a₁`, the conic is equivalent to `w² = u x² + p v y²` with the `p`-adic units
`u = −bc`, `v = −a₁ b`, and `Qp.hilbertSolvable_unit_pv_iff` applies.
nodes.type:
∀ {p : Nat} [hP : Foundations.Langlands.Padic.PrimeP p],
  p % 2 = 1 →
    ∀ {a b c : Int},
      ↑p ∣ a →
        Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Legendre.Squarefree a →
          ¬↑p ∣ b →
            ¬↑p ∣ c →
              Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Legendre.ConicSolvableQp p a b c →
                Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Legendre.IsSqMod (-(b * c)) ↑p

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Computability.tvalid_iff
nodes.doc:
Unfolding validity: a tree is valid iff its root follows by a rule from the roots of
its subtrees, and all subtrees are smaller and valid.
nodes.type:
∀ (step : Nat → Nat → Nat → Bool) (t : Nat),
  Foundations.Logic.Computability.tvalid step t = 1 ↔
    step (Foundations.Logic.Computability.troot t)
          (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd (Foundations.Logic.Computability.fst t))
          (Foundations.Logic.Computability.fst (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd t)) =
        true ∧
      Foundations.Logic.Computability.llen
            (Foundations.Logic.Computability.fst (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd t)) =
          Foundations.Logic.Computability.llen
            (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd t)) ∧
        ∀ (i : Nat),
          i <
              Foundations.Logic.Computability.llen
                (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd t)) →
            Foundations.Logic.Computability.lnth
                  (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd t)) i <
                t ∧
              Foundations.Logic.Computability.tvalid step
                    (Foundations.Logic.Computability.lnth
                      (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd (Foundations.Logic.Computability.snd t)) i) =
                  1 ∧
                Foundations.Logic.Computability.troot

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.R.ordered_field
nodes.doc:
**ℝ is an ordered field.** The field laws hold, every non-zero real has an inverse, and `≤`
is a linear order compatible with addition and with multiplication by positive reals.
nodes.type:
(∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.R), x + y + z = x + (y + z)) ∧
  (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.R), x + y = y + x) ∧
    (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), x + 0 = x) ∧
      (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), -x + x = 0) ∧
        (∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.R), x * y * z = x * (y * z)) ∧
          (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.R), x * y = y * x) ∧
            (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), x * 1 = x) ∧
              (∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.R), x * (y + z) = x * y + x * z) ∧
                0 ≠ 1 ∧
                  (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), x ≠ 0 → x * x⁻¹ = 1) ∧
                    (∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.R), x ≤ y → y ≤ z → x ≤ z) ∧
                      (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.R), x ≤ y → y ≤ x → x = y) ∧
                        (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.R), x ≤ y ∨ y ≤ x) ∧
                          (∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.R), x ≤ y → x + z ≤ y + z) ∧
                            ∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.R), x < y → 0 < z → z * x < z * y

(`hi_{j+1} ≤ lo_j ≤ hi_j`, `hi_0 ≤ N`), then
`Σ_{j < J} Σ_{lo_j < k ≤ hi_j} g(k) ≤ Σ_{k ≤ N} g(k)` (block sums written as differences of
partial sums).
nodes.type:
∀ (g : Nat → Foundations.Numbers.R) {N : Nat},
  (∀ (k : Nat), k ≤ N → 0 ≤ g k) →
    ∀ (lo hi : Nat → Nat),
      (∀ (j : Nat), lo j ≤ hi j) →
        (∀ (j : Nat), hi (j + 1) ≤ lo j) →
          hi 0 ≤ N →
            ∀ (J : Nat),
              Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum
                  (fun j => Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum g (hi j + 1) - Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum g (lo j + 1)) J ≤
                Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum g (N + 1)

  Foundations.Langlands.natInv (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card G) *
      Foundations.Langlands.pairing (Foundations.Langlands.character (Foundations.Langlands.indRep H σ))
        (Foundations.Langlands.character ρ) =
    Foundations.Langlands.natInv (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card { x // x ∈ H }) *

`g` and continuous reparametrisations `φ, ψ` with the same values at `0` and `1`, then `P` and `Q`

∀ {X : Type} [inst : Foundations.Topology.MetricSpace X] {x y : X} {g : Foundations.Numbers.R → X},
  Foundations.Topology.Continuous g →
    ∀ {φ ψ : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R},
      Foundations.Topology.Continuous φ →
        Foundations.Topology.Continuous ψ →
          φ 0 = ψ 0 →
            φ 1 = ψ 1 →
              ∀ (P Q : Foundations.Topology.Path x y),
                (∀ (t : Foundations.Numbers.R), 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → P.toFun t = g (φ t)) →
                  (∀ (t : Foundations.Numbers.R), 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → Q.toFun t = g (ψ t)) → P.Homotopic Q

not all of the same sign and `−bc`, `−ca`, `−ab` are squares modulo `|a|`, `|b|`, `|c|`.

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Computability.incompleteness
nodes.doc:
**Abstract incompleteness theorem** (computational form of Gödel's first
incompleteness theorem; *abstract* — see the module docstring for exactly which
hypotheses remain to be discharged for a concrete system such as PA).

Let `Provable c x` mean "the formal system proves that code `c` does not halt on
input `x`". Suppose the system is
* **sound** for such statements: it proves only true ones; and
* **computably enumerable**: some code `q` halts on `(⌜c⌝, x)` exactly when
  `Provable c x`.

Then the system is **incomplete**: there is an explicit code `c` and input `x` such
that `c` does not halt on `x`, yet this is not provable. Namely `c = godelCode q` and
`x = ⌜c⌝` — the statement "I am not provable", in computational dress.
nodes.type:
∀ (Provable : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code → Nat → Prop),
  (∀ (c : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code) (x : Nat),
      Provable c x → ¬Foundations.Logic.Computability.Halts c [x]) →
    ∀ {q : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code},
      (∀ (c : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code) (x : Nat),
          Foundations.Logic.Computability.Halts q [Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode c, x] ↔ Provable c x) →
        ¬Foundations.Logic.Computability.Halts (Foundations.Logic.Computability.godelCode q)
              [Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode (Foundations.Logic.Computability.godelCode q)] ∧
          ¬Provable (Foundations.Logic.Computability.godelCode q)
              (Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode (Foundations.Logic.Computability.godelCode q))

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.multiplicity_eq
nodes.doc:
**Multiplicities from characters.** Let `ρ₀, …, ρ_{r−1}` be pairwise non-isomorphic
irreducible representations over an algebraically closed field in which their degrees are
non-zero. If `χ = Σ_k m_k χ_{ρ_k}` then `Σ_g χ(g) χ_{ρⱼ}(g⁻¹) = m_j |G|`.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G] {K : Type w}
  [inst_2 : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing K] {r : Nat} {ιs : Fin r → Type v}
  [inst_3 : (k : Fin r) → Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType (ιs k)],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField K →
    Foundations.Langlands.AlgClosed K →
      ∀ (ρs : (k : Fin r) → Foundations.Langlands.Rep G K (ιs k)),
        (∀ (k : Fin r), Foundations.Langlands.Irreducible (ρs k)) →
          (∀ (k k' : Fin r), k ≠ k' → ¬Foundations.Langlands.Iso (ρs k) (ρs k')) →
            (∀ (k : Fin r), Foundations.Algebra.ncast (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card (ιs k)) ≠ 0) →
              ∀ (m : Fin r → Nat) (χ : G → K),
                (∀ (g : G),
                    χ g =
                      Foundations.Algebra.isum fun k =>
                        Foundations.Algebra.ncast (m k) * Foundations.Langlands.character (ρs k) g) →
                  ∀ (j : Fin r),
                    Foundations.Langlands.pairing χ (Foundations.Langlands.character (ρs j)) =
                      Foundations.Algebra.ncast (m j) *
                        Foundations.Algebra.ncast (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card G)

**Bridge theorem (ℤ).** The equivalence `Z ≃ Int` preserves `0`, `1`, addition, negation,
multiplication and order. So the integers built from pairs of naturals are the same structure as
Lean's `Int`, and we use `Int` from now on.

  Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun 1 = 1 ∧
    (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
        Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun (x + y) =
          Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun x + Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun y) ∧
      (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
          Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun (-x) = -Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun x) ∧
        (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
            Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun (x * y) =
              Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun x * Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun y) ∧
          ∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Z),
            x ≤ y ↔ Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun x ≤ Foundations.Numbers.Z.equivInt.toFun y

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.dline_transport
nodes.doc:
**Transporting a justified line.** If the entries `0, …, j` of `(c₁, d₁)` reappear in
`(c, d)` at positions `s + p`, all of them before `K` for `p < j`, and the entry `j`
reappears at `K`, then a justified line `j` of `(c₁, d₁)` is a justified line `K` of
`(c, d)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {N : Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel} {c₁ d₁ c d s j K : N.Dom},
  (∀ (p y : N.Dom),
      p ≤ j → Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c₁ d₁ p y → Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c d (s + p) y) →
    (∀ (p : N.Dom), p < j → s + p < K) →
      (∀ (y : N.Dom), Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c₁ d₁ j y → Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c d K y) →
        Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.DLineM c₁ d₁ j → Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.DLineM c d K

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.mobius_identity
nodes.doc: **The Möbius identity.** `log N + S_χ(N) = Σ_{d ≤ N} χ(d) μ(d) (log N − log d)/d · Σ_{m ≤ N/d} χ(m)/m`.

  Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal (Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat N) + Foundations.NumberTheory.chebSum χ N =
    Foundations.Numbers.gsum
      (fun d =>
        Foundations.NumberTheory.dchar χ d *
            Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal
              (Foundations.NumberTheory.mobius d * (Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat N - Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat d) /
                ↑d) *
          Foundations.NumberTheory.lpart (Foundations.NumberTheory.dchar χ) (N / d + 1))
      (N + 1)

nodes.name: Foundations.Sets.ZFSet.recursion_theorem
nodes.doc:
**Dedekind's recursion theorem.** Let `a ∈ A` and let `g` map `A` into `A`.
Then there is exactly one function `F` from `ω` to `A` (a set of pairs) with
`F(∅) = a` and `F(succ n) = g(F(n))` for all `n ∈ ω`.
nodes.type:
∀ {A a : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet},
  a ∈ A →
    ∀ (g : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet → Foundations.Sets.ZFSet),
      (∀ (x : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), x ∈ A → g x ∈ A) →
        ∃ F,
          F.IsFunction ω A ∧
            F.app ∅ = a ∧
              (∀ (n : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), n ∈ ω → F.app n.succ = g (F.app n)) ∧
                ∀ (G : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet),
                  G.IsFunction ω A →
                    G.app ∅ = a → (∀ (n : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet), n ∈ ω → G.app n.succ = g (G.app n)) → G = F

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.Ascoli.arzela_ascoli
nodes.doc:
**Arzelà–Ascoli theorem.** A uniformly bounded, equicontinuous sequence of functions on
`[a, b]` has a subsequence converging uniformly on `[a, b]`.
nodes.type:
∀ {fs : Nat → Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R} {a b : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  a ≤ b →
    (∃ B, ∀ (n : Nat) (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), a ≤ x → x ≤ b → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (fs n x) ≤ B) →
      (∀ (ε : Foundations.Numbers.R),
          0 < ε →
            ∃ δ,
              0 < δ ∧
                ∀ (n : Nat) (x y : Foundations.Numbers.R),
                  a ≤ x →
                    x ≤ b →
                      a ≤ y →
                        y ≤ b →
                          Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (x - y) < δ → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (fs n x - fs n y) < ε) →
        ∃ φ,
          (∀ (k : Nat), φ k < φ (k + 1)) ∧ ∃ g, Foundations.Topology.UnifOn (fun k => fs (φ k)) g fun x => a ≤ x ∧ x ≤ b

nodes.type:

  Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Measurable S f →
    (∀ (x : α), 0 ≤ f x) →
      ∀ {δ : Foundations.Numbers.R},
        0 < δ →
          ∀ (K : Nat),
            (∀ (l : Foundations.Numbers.R × Foundations.Numbers.R × (α → Prop)),
                l ∈ Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.levels f δ K → S.M l.snd.snd) ∧
              Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.DisjOn (fun l => l.snd.snd)
                  (Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.levels f δ K) ∧
                (∀ (x : α),
                    Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.UnionOf (fun l => l.snd.snd)
                      (Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.levels f δ K) x) ∧
                  ∀ (l : Foundations.Numbers.R × Foundations.Numbers.R × (α → Prop)),
                    l ∈ Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.levels f δ K →
                      0 ≤ l.fst ∧
                        l.snd.fst = l.fst + δ ∧
                          ∀ (x : α), l.snd.snd x → l.fst ≤ f x ∧ (f x < l.snd.fst ∨ ↑K * δ ≤ l.fst)

**The determination lemma.** If `1 = λp + μq`, `p = λ + μγ`, `q = λγ + μ` with

  0 ≤ l →
    0 < m →
      1 < g →
        0 ≤ l' →
          0 < m' →
            1 < g' →
              1 = l * p + m * q →
                p = l + m * g →
                  q = l * g + m → 1 = l' * p + m' * q → p = l' + m' * g' → q = l' * g' + m' → l = l' ∧ m = m'

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.monoRep
nodes.doc:
**Monomial representation.** Given `ζ` with `ζ^m = 1`, permutations `P_g` of `Fin n` and
exponents `E_g : Fin n → Fin m` with `P_1 = id`, `E_1 = 0` and the cocycle rules
`P_{gh} = P_g ∘ P_h`, `E_{gh}(j) = E_g(P_h(j)) + E_h(j)`, the matrices
`ρ(g) : e_j ↦ ζ^{E_g(j)} e_{P_g(j)}` form a representation of `G` on `K^n`.
nodes.type:
{K : Type w} →
  [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing K] →
    {n : Nat} →
      {G : Type u} →
        [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] →
          {m : Nat} →
            (ζ : K) →
              Foundations.Langlands.cpow ζ m = 1 →
                (P : G → Fin n → Fin n) →
                  (E : G → Fin n → Fin m) →
                    (∀ (j : Fin n), P 1 j = j ∧ ↑(E 1 j) = 0) →
                      (∀ (g h : G) (j : Fin n), P (g * h) j = P g (P h j) ∧ E (g * h) j = E g (P h j) + E h j) →
                        Foundations.Langlands.Rep G K (Fin n)

**The key estimate.** For disjoint measurable `Eₙ` with union `U` and any test set `T`:
the series `Σ ν(T ∩ Eₙ)` converges to some `s` with `s + ν(T ∖ U) ≤ ν(T)` and `ν(T ∩ U) ≤ s`.

  (∀ (n : Nat), o.IsMeasurable (E n)) →
    Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.Disjoint E →
      ∀ (T : α → Prop),
        ∃ s,
          Foundations.Numbers.R.HasSum (fun n => o.ν fun x => T x ∧ E n x) s ∧
            (s + o.ν fun x => T x ∧ ¬∃ n, E n x) ≤ o.ν T ∧ (o.ν fun x => T x ∧ ∃ n, E n x) ≤ s

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.N.bridge_nat

and preserves addition, multiplication and order. Hence the home-made natural numbers and Lean's
`Nat` are the same structure, and we may use `Nat` from now on.

  (∀ (n : Foundations.Numbers.N),
      Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun n.succ = Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun n + 1) ∧
    (∀ (a b : Foundations.Numbers.N),
        Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun (a + b) =
          Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun a + Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun b) ∧
      (∀ (a b : Foundations.Numbers.N),
          Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun (a * b) =
            Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun a * Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun b) ∧
        ∀ (a b : Foundations.Numbers.N),
          a ≤ b ↔ Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun a ≤ Foundations.Numbers.N.equivNat.toFun b

        ∀ (φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith),
          Foundations.Logic.Computability.Halts c [Foundations.Logic.FO.fcode φ] ↔ T ⊢₁ φ) →
      ¬T ⊢₁ Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.bot → ∃ σ, Foundations.Logic.FO.IsSentence σ ∧ ¬T ⊢₁ σ ∧ ¬T ⊢₁ σ.neg

`μ(p² e) = 0` on both sides. (At `n = 0`, outside the range where `μ` is meaningful, the two
conventions differ: the empty-ish product gives `PNT.mobius 0 = 1`, while `mobius 0 = 0`.)

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.eisenstein_irreducible
nodes.doc:
**Eisenstein's criterion.** Let `f ∈ ℚ[x]` (`ℚ` the prime field of a field `Ω` of
characteristic zero) have integer coefficients `F₀, …, Fₙ` with `Fₙ = 1` and `n ≥ 1`. If a prime
`p` divides `F₀, …, F_{n-1}` and `p² ∤ F₀`, then `f` is irreducible in `ℚ[x]`.
nodes.type:
∀ {Ω : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing Ω] (hΩ : Foundations.Algebra.IsField Ω)
  (hc : Foundations.Algebra.CharZero Ω) {p : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
    ∀ (f : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial { x // x ∈ Foundations.Algebra.ratField hΩ hc }) {F : Nat → Int} {n : Nat},
      1 ≤ n →
        (∀ (k : Nat), (f.coeff k).val = ↑(F k)) →
          Foundations.Algebra.SuppLE F n →
            F n = 1 → (∀ (k : Nat), k < n → ↑p ∣ F k) → ¬↑p * ↑p ∣ F 0 → Foundations.Algebra.Irreducible f

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.le_bprod_of_pow_dvd

**Bounding a number by its prime-power divisors.** Suppose every prime factor of `m > 0`
is below `B`, and every prime power `pᵉ` dividing `m` is at most `f(p)`, where all `f(i) ≥ 1`.

  0 < m →
    (∀ (i : Nat), 1 ≤ f i) →
      (∀ (p e : Nat), Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p → p ^ e ∣ m → p ^ e ≤ f p) →
        (∀ (p : Nat), Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p → p ∣ m → p < B) → m ≤ Foundations.NumberTheory.bprod f B

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.R.abs_rsum_sub_rsum_le
nodes.doc:
**Comparison lemma.** If `|f s − f s'| ≤ ε` whenever `s, s' ∈ [A, B]` are within `2δ`, then
the Riemann sums over any two `δ`-fine partitions of `[a, b]` differ by at most `ε (b − a)`.
Proof: walk along both partitions simultaneously, each time cutting off the shorter of the two
first pieces.
nodes.type:
∀ {f : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R} {A B δ ε : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  (∀ (s s' : Foundations.Numbers.R),
      A ≤ s →
        s ≤ B →
          A ≤ s' → s' ≤ B → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (s - s') < 2 * δ → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (f s - f s') ≤ ε) →
    ∀ (n : Nat) (a b : Foundations.Numbers.R) (P Q : List (Foundations.Numbers.R × Foundations.Numbers.R)),
      P.length + Q.length ≤ n →
        A.Fine B δ a P b →
          A.Fine B δ a Q b →
            Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (Foundations.Numbers.R.rsum f a P - Foundations.Numbers.R.rsum f a Q) ≤
              ε * (b - a)

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.dedekind
nodes.doc:
**Dedekind's lemma on the independence of characters.** Pairwise distinct maps
`χ₁, …, χₙ : F → F` into a field that are multiplicative (`χ(xy) = χ(x)χ(y)`, `χ(1) = 1`) are
linearly independent over `F`: if `∑ cᵢ χᵢ(x) = 0` for all `x`, then every `cᵢ = 0`.
nodes.type:
∀ {F : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing F],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField F →
    ∀ (n : Nat) (χ : Fin n → F → F),
      (∀ (i : Fin n) (x y : F), χ i (x * y) = χ i x * χ i y) →
        (∀ (i : Fin n), χ i 1 = 1) →
          (∀ (i j : Fin n), χ i = χ j → i = j) →
            ∀ (c : Fin n → F), (∀ (x : F), (Foundations.Algebra.isum fun i => c i * χ i x) = 0) → ∀ (i : Fin n), c i = 0

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Padic.newton_step_strong
nodes.doc:

`p^(2e+1+n) ∣ f(s)`, then the corrected point `s + (−(f(s)/p^(2e+1+n)) u) p^(e+1+n)` satisfies

  Foundations.Langlands.Padic.pderiv f s = ↑p ^ e * w →
    ↑p ∣ u * w - 1 →
      ↑p ^ (2 * e + 1 + n) ∣ Foundations.Langlands.Padic.peval f s →
        ↑p ^ (2 * e + 2 + n) ∣
          Foundations.Langlands.Padic.peval f
            (s + -(Foundations.Langlands.Padic.peval f s / ↑p ^ (2 * e + 1 + n)) * u * ↑p ^ (e + 1 + n))

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial.unique_factorization
nodes.doc:
**Unique factorisation in `F[x]`.** Over a field, every non-zero non-unit polynomial is a
product of irreducible polynomials, uniquely up to order and constant factors.
nodes.type:
∀ {F : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing F],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField F →
    ∀ (p : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial F),
      p ≠ 0 →
        ¬Foundations.Algebra.IsUnit p →
          (∃ L,
              (∀ (q : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial F), q ∈ L → Foundations.Algebra.Irreducible q) ∧
                Foundations.Algebra.lprod L = p) ∧
            ∀ (L M : List (Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial F)),
              (∀ (q : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial F), q ∈ L → Foundations.Algebra.Irreducible q) →
                (∀ (q : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial F), q ∈ M → Foundations.Algebra.Irreducible q) →
                  Foundations.Algebra.lprod L = p →
                    Foundations.Algebra.lprod M = p →
                      ∀ (x : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial F),
                        Foundations.Algebra.countAssoc x L = Foundations.Algebra.countAssoc x M

object, a product and a natural numbers object.

    Foundations.Bridges.El.map F = Foundations.Bridges.El.map G → F = G) ∧
  (∀ {X Y : Foundations.Bridges.ZFCat}
      (f : Foundations.Categories.Category.Hom (Foundations.Bridges.El.obj X) (Foundations.Bridges.El.obj Y)),
      ∃ F, Foundations.Bridges.El.map F = f) ∧
    (¬∃ X, Nonempty (Foundations.Categories.Iso (Foundations.Bridges.El.obj X) Foundations.Sets.ZFSet)) ∧
      Nonempty (Foundations.Categories.IsTerminal (Foundations.Bridges.El.obj Foundations.Bridges.zfOne)) ∧
        (∀ (X Y : Foundations.Bridges.ZFCat),
            Nonempty
              (Foundations.Categories.IsProduct (Foundations.Bridges.El.obj X) (Foundations.Bridges.El.obj Y)
                (Foundations.Bridges.El.obj (Foundations.Bridges.zfProd X Y))
                (Foundations.Bridges.El.map (Foundations.Bridges.zfFst X Y))
                (Foundations.Bridges.El.map (Foundations.Bridges.zfSnd X Y)))) ∧
          Nonempty
            (Foundations.Categories.IsNNO (Foundations.Bridges.El.obj Foundations.Bridges.zfOne)

impossible: an irreducible factor of `P̄` would be a repeated factor of `xⁿ - 1` in `𝔽_p[x]`.
nodes.type:

        1 ≤ d →
          Foundations.Langlands.Monic P d →
            Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial.X ^ n + -1 = P * Q * S →
              (Foundations.Langlands.powSubst p).toFun Q = P * T → False

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.tarski_undefinability

**Tarski's undefinability theorem.** No formula `Tr(x)` (with only the free
variable `x`) defines arithmetical truth: there is no `Tr` such that, for every
sentence `σ`, `ℕ ⊨ Tr(⌜σ⌝)` iff `ℕ ⊨ σ`.
nodes.type:
¬∃ Tr,
    (∀ (x : Nat), 1 ≤ x → Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Fresh x Tr) ∧
      ∀ (σ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith),
        Foundations.Logic.FO.IsSentence σ →
          ∀ (e : Nat → Nat),
            Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat Foundations.Logic.FO.stdModel e
                (Tr.inst (Foundations.Logic.FO.numeral (Foundations.Logic.FO.fcode σ))) ↔
              Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat Foundations.Logic.FO.stdModel e σ

nodes.doc:
**Padding an interval with zeros.** If `[a, a + ℓ) ⊆ [b, b + ℓ')`, then summing `h` over the
small interval is the same as summing over the large one the function equal to `h` on the
small interval and to `0` elsewhere.

∀ {α : Type} [inst : Lean.Grind.Field α] {a b : Int} {len len' : Nat},
  b ≤ a →

      ∀ (h : Int → α),
        (Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.isum b len' fun n => if a ≤ n ∧ n < a + ↑len then h n else 0) =
          Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.isum a len h

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.gsum_vonMangoldt_mul
nodes.doc:
**Regrouping a `Λ`-weighted sum by prime powers.**
`Σ_{n ≤ N} Λ(n) g(n) = Σ_{p ≤ N} Σ_{k ≤ N} [p prime, k ≥ 1, pᵏ ≤ N] · log p · g(pᵏ)`.
nodes.type:
∀ (g : Nat → Foundations.Numbers.R) (N : Nat),
  Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun n => Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt n * g n) (N + 1) =
    Foundations.Numbers.gsum
      (fun p =>
        Foundations.Numbers.gsum
          (fun k =>
            if Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p ∧ 1 ≤ k ∧ p ^ k ≤ N then Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat p * g (p ^ k)
            else 0)
          (N + 1))
      (N + 1)

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.cabs_lnat_add_chebSum_le
nodes.doc: **If `L(1, χ) = 0` then `S_χ(N) = −log N + O(1)`**: precisely `|log N + S_χ(N)| ≤ 2q`.
nodes.type:
∀ {q : Nat} [inst : NeZero q] (χ : Foundations.NumberTheory.Character (Foundations.Algebra.ZModUnits q)),
  χ ≠ Foundations.NumberTheory.Character.one →

      ∀ {N : Nat},
        0 < N →
          (Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal (Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat N) + Foundations.NumberTheory.chebSum χ N).cabs ≤
            2 * ↑q

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.brouwer_one_dim

nodes.name: Foundations.Probability.FinProb.Var_sumN

variables is the sum of their variances.

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Computability.halting_undecidable
nodes.doc:
**Undecidability of the halting problem** (Turing 1936). There is no code `h`
that is total on (Gödel numbers of codes, inputs) and outputs `1` when `c` halts on
`x` and `0` when it does not.
nodes.type:
¬∃ h,
    ∀ (c : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code) (x : Nat),
      (Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval h [Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode c, x] 0 ∨
          Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval h [Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode c, x] 1) ∧
        (Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval h [Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode c, x] 1 ↔
          Foundations.Logic.Computability.Halts c [x])

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing R],

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.selberg_symmetry
nodes.doc:
**Selberg's symmetry formula.** For every `N ≥ 1`,
`|ψ(N) log N + Σ_{n ≤ N} Λ(n) ψ(⌊N/n⌋) − 2N log N| ≤ (30 + 3 log 1024) · N`,
i.e. `ψ(x) log x + Σ_{n ≤ x} Λ(n) ψ(x/n) = 2x log x + O(x)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {N : Nat},
  1 ≤ N →
    Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs
        (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.psi N * (↑N).log +
            Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum
              (fun n => Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vonMangoldt n * Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.psi (N / n)) (N + 1) -
          2 * ↑N * (↑N).log) ≤
      (30 + 3 * Foundations.Numbers.R.log 1024) * ↑N

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.gaussSum_sq
nodes.doc:
**Gauss's theorem on the square of the Gauss sum.** If `ζ^p = 1` and
`1 + ζ + ⋯ + ζ^{p-1} = 0` in a commutative ring, then `g² = (-1/p) · p = p*`.
nodes.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing R] {p : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
    p % 2 = 1 →
      ∀ {ζ : R},
        ζ ^ p = 1 →
          Foundations.Algebra.rsum (fun j => ζ ^ j) p = 0 →
            Foundations.Langlands.gaussSum p ζ * Foundations.Langlands.gaussSum p ζ = ↑(Foundations.Langlands.pstar p)

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.good_interval
nodes.doc:
**Good intervals.** For every `ε > 0` there are `K, T ≥ 1` and `y₀` such that for every
`y ≥ y₀` some `m ∈ (y, Ky]` has `|V(n)| ≤ ε/2` for all `n ∈ [m, m + ⌊m/T⌋]`.
nodes.type:
∀ {ε : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  0 < ε →
    ∃ K T y₀,
      1 ≤ K ∧
        1 ≤ T ∧
          ∀ (y : Nat),
            y₀ ≤ y →
              ∃ m,
                y < m ∧
                  m ≤ K * y ∧
                    ∀ (n : Nat),
                      m ≤ n → n ≤ m + m / T → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vrem n) ≤ ε / 2

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.C.exists_min_on_square
nodes.doc:

∀ {g : Foundations.Numbers.C → Foundations.Numbers.R} {ρ : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  0 ≤ ρ →
    (∀ (z : Foundations.Numbers.C), 0 ≤ g z) →
      (∀ (z₀ : Foundations.Numbers.C) (ε : Foundations.Numbers.R),
          0 < ε →
            ∃ δ,
              0 < δ ∧ ∀ (z : Foundations.Numbers.C), (z - z₀).cabs < δ → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (g z - g z₀) < ε) →
        ∃ zs,
          Foundations.Numbers.C.InSq ρ zs ∧ ∀ (z : Foundations.Numbers.C), Foundations.Numbers.C.InSq ρ z → g zs ≤ g z

  Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.count Q = n →
    (∀ (y : X), Q y → Foundations.Algebra.MulAction.orbit G x y) →
      (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.count fun g => Q (g • x)) =
        n * Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.count fun x_1 => x_1 ∈ Foundations.Algebra.MulAction.stabilizer G x

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.abel_bound
nodes.doc:
**Abel's summation by parts.** If `|Σ_{n<N} a(n)| ≤ B` for all `N`, and `b ≥ 0` is
non-increasing from `M` on, then `|Σ_{M ≤ n < K} a(n) b(n)| ≤ 2 B b(M)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {a : Nat → Foundations.Numbers.C} {B : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  (∀ (N : Nat), (Foundations.Numbers.gsum a N).cabs ≤ B) →
    ∀ {b : Nat → Foundations.Numbers.R} {M : Nat},
      (∀ (n : Nat), M ≤ n → b (n + 1) ≤ b n) →
        (∀ (n : Nat), M ≤ n → 0 ≤ b n) →
          ∀ (K : Nat),
            M ≤ K →
              (Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun n => a n * Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal (b n)) K -
                    Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun n => a n * Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal (b n)) M).cabs ≤
                2 * B * b M
