nodes.name: Foundations.Forcing.ccc_iSup_countable
nodes.doc:
**Every supremum in a ccc algebra is a countable supremum.** If `B` is ccc, then for every
family `(bᵢ)_{i ∈ ι}` there is a countable subfamily with the same supremum.

Proof: by Zorn's lemma take a maximal family `M` of pairwise disjoint non-zero elements, each
below some `bᵢ`; it is countable by ccc. Choosing such an `i` for each member of `M` gives a
countable subfamily. If its supremum `T` were below `⨆ᵢ bᵢ` and different from it, some
`bᵢ ⊓ Tᶜ` would be non-zero and could be added to `M`.

This is the algebraic core of the standard proof that ccc forcing preserves cardinals: a
name for a function from `ω` into a ground-model set has, at each argument, only countably
many possible values. That set-theoretic consequence is **not** formalised here.
nodes.type:
∀ {B : Type} [inst : Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra B],
  Foundations.Forcing.IsCCC B →
    ∀ {ι : Type} (b : ι → B),
      ∃ J j,
        Foundations.Sets.Countable J ∧ Foundations.Forcing.CBA.iSup b = Foundations.Forcing.CBA.iSup fun k => b (j k)

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.frobenius_fixes_sqrtField_iff_pstar_sq
nodes.doc:
**The decomposition law of `ℚ(√p*)`, via Frobenius.** Let `p, q` be distinct odd primes and
`σ_q : ζ_p ↦ ζ_p^q` the Frobenius automorphism of `ℚ(ζ_p)` at `q`. Then `σ_q` fixes the quadratic
subfield `ℚ(√p*)` pointwise if and only if `p* = (-1)^((p-1)/2) p` is a square modulo `q`.
(Classically: `q` splits in `ℚ(√p*)` iff `p*` is a square mod `q`. Prime ideals are not
formalised in this library, so splitting is expressed here only through `σ_q`.)
nodes.type:
∀ {p q : Nat} (hp : Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p) (hodd : p % 2 = 1),
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime q →
    q % 2 = 1 →
      p ≠ q →
        ∀ (hpq' : ¬p ∣ q),
          (∀ (x : { x // x ∈ Foundations.Langlands.cycloField hp }),
              x.val ∈ Foundations.Langlands.sqrtField hp hodd → (Foundations.Langlands.galAut hp hpq').toFun x = x) ↔
            Foundations.Langlands.IsSqMod (Foundations.Langlands.pstar p) q

`f(a) ≡ 0 (mod p)` and `f'(a) ≢ 0 (mod p)`, then there is a `p`-adic integer `x` with `f(x) = 0`
and `x ≡ a (mod p)`.

∀ {p : Nat},

          ∃ x, Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp.peval f x = 0 ∧ Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp.ModPow 1 x ↑a

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.improve
nodes.doc:
**The improvement lemma.** For every `ε > 0` there is `δ > 0` such that: whenever
`ε ≤ α ≤ C₀` and `|V(n)| ≤ α` for all large `n`, then `|V(n)| ≤ α − δ` for all large `n`.
nodes.type:
∀ {ε : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  0 < ε →
    ∃ δ,
      0 < δ ∧
        ∀ (α : Foundations.Numbers.R),
          ε ≤ α →
            α ≤ Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.C0 →
              ∀ (N₀ : Nat),
                (∀ (n : Nat), N₀ ≤ n → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vrem n) ≤ α) →
                  ∃ N₁, ∀ (N : Nat), N₁ ≤ N → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vrem N) ≤ α - δ

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.mem_of_ortho
nodes.doc:
**Every character occurs in an orthogonal family.** If `L` is a non-empty list of characters
with `Σ_{ψ ∈ L} ψ(x) = |L| · [x = 1]`, then every character `χ` belongs to `L`: otherwise each
`ψ · χ̄` would be a non-trivial character, so `Σ_x Σ_ψ ψ(x) χ(x⁻¹) = 0`, while summing in the
other order gives `|L|`.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommGroup G] [Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G]
  {L : List (G → Foundations.Numbers.C)},
  L ≠ [] →
    (∀ (ψ : G → Foundations.Numbers.C), ψ ∈ L → Foundations.NumberTheory.IsChar ψ) →
      (∀ (x : G), (Foundations.NumberTheory.lsum L fun ψ => ψ x) = if x = 1 then ↑L.length else 0) →
        ∀ {χ : G → Foundations.Numbers.C}, Foundations.NumberTheory.IsChar χ → χ ∈ L

with `0 ≠ 1`.

  (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Z), x + y = y + x) ∧

      (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.Z), -x + x = 0) ∧
        (∀ (x y z : Foundations.Numbers.Z), x * y * z = x * (y * z)) ∧
          (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Z), x * y = y * x) ∧
            (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.Z), x * 1 = x) ∧

nodes.name: Foundations.Forcing.isFunc_inf_isInj_eq_bot
nodes.doc:
**Preservation of cardinals by ccc forcing.** Let `X = {h t | t ∈ T}` and
`Y = {k u | u ∈ U}` be names (all members with degree `⊤`) whose members `h t` are pairwise
Boolean-distinct. If `T` does not inject into `U × ℕ`, then in `V^B` (for ccc `B`) no `f` is an
injective function from `X` into `Y`: `⟦f is a function X → Y⟧ ⊓ ⟦f is injective on X⟧ = ⊥`.
nodes.type:
∀ {B : Type} [inst : Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra B],
  Foundations.Forcing.IsCCC B →
    ∀ {T U : Type} (h : T → Foundations.Forcing.BSet B) (k : U → Foundations.Forcing.BSet B),
      (∀ (t t' : T), t ≠ t' → (h t).eq (h t') = Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.bot) →
        (¬∃ g, Function.Injective g) →
          ∀ (f : Foundations.Forcing.BSet B),
            Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.inf
                (f.isFunc (Foundations.Forcing.BSet.mk T h fun x => Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.top)
                  (Foundations.Forcing.BSet.mk U k fun x => Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.top))
                (f.isInj (Foundations.Forcing.BSet.mk T h fun x => Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.top)) =
              Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.bot

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.multiplicity_eq_inner
nodes.doc:
**Multiplicity as an inner product.** Under the hypotheses of `multiplicity_eq`, with
`t = |G|⁻¹`: `m_j = ⟨χ, χ_j⟩ = t · Σ_g χ(g) χ_j(g⁻¹)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G] {K : Type w}
  [inst_2 : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing K] {r : Nat} {ιs : Fin r → Type v}
  [inst_3 : (k : Fin r) → Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType (ιs k)],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField K →
    Foundations.Langlands.AlgClosed K →
      ∀ (ρs : (k : Fin r) → Foundations.Langlands.Rep G K (ιs k)),
        (∀ (k : Fin r), Foundations.Langlands.Irreducible (ρs k)) →
          (∀ (k k' : Fin r), k ≠ k' → ¬Foundations.Langlands.Iso (ρs k) (ρs k')) →
            (∀ (k : Fin r), Foundations.Algebra.ncast (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card (ιs k)) ≠ 0) →
              ∀ (m : Fin r → Nat) (χ : G → K),
                (∀ (g : G),
                    χ g =
                      Foundations.Algebra.isum fun k =>
                        Foundations.Algebra.ncast (m k) * Foundations.Langlands.character (ρs k) g) →
                  ∀ (j : Fin r) {t : K},
                    Foundations.Algebra.ncast (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card G) * t = 1 →
                      t * Foundations.Langlands.pairing χ (Foundations.Langlands.character (ρs j)) =
                        Foundations.Algebra.ncast (m j)

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Forms.Form.classNumber_spec
nodes.doc:
**The class number counts classes.** For `D < 0`, `h(D)` is the length of a duplicate-free
list of primitive positive definite forms of discriminant `D` such that every primitive
positive definite form of discriminant `D` is properly equivalent to exactly one entry.
nodes.type:
∀ {D : Int},
  D < 0 →
    Foundations.Langlands.Forms.Form.classNumber D = (Foundations.Langlands.Forms.Form.primReducedForms D).length ∧
      (Foundations.Langlands.Forms.Form.primReducedForms D).Nodup ∧
        (∀ (g : Foundations.Langlands.Forms.Form),
            g ∈ Foundations.Langlands.Forms.Form.primReducedForms D → g.PosDef ∧ g.disc = D ∧ g.Primitive) ∧
          ∀ (f : Foundations.Langlands.Forms.Form),
            f.PosDef →
              f.disc = D →
                f.Primitive →
                  ∃ g,
                    g ∈ Foundations.Langlands.Forms.Form.primReducedForms D ∧
                      f.Equiv g ∧
                        ∀ (g' : Foundations.Langlands.Forms.Form),
                          g' ∈ Foundations.Langlands.Forms.Form.primReducedForms D → f.Equiv g' → g' = g

nodes.name: Foundations.Categories.lawvere_fixed_point
nodes.doc:
**Lawvere's fixed-point theorem.** Let `A × A` be a product (projections `p₁, p₂`)
and `φ : A × A ⟶ B` be point-surjective with respect to `T`-points: for every
`g : A ⟶ B` there is `a : T ⟶ A` with `φ ∘ ⟨a, x⟩ = g ∘ x` for all `x : T ⟶ A`. Then every
`t : B ⟶ B` has a fixed `T`-point `b : T ⟶ B`, `b ≫ t = b`.
nodes.type:
∀ {C : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Categories.Category C] {A B AA T : C}
  {p₁ p₂ : Foundations.Categories.Category.Hom AA A} (hP : Foundations.Categories.IsProduct A A AA p₁ p₂)
  (φ : Foundations.Categories.Category.Hom AA B),
  (∀ (g : Foundations.Categories.Category.Hom A B),
      ∃ a,
        ∀ (x : Foundations.Categories.Category.Hom T A),
          Foundations.Categories.Category.comp (hP.lift a x) φ = Foundations.Categories.Category.comp x g) →
    ∀ (t : Foundations.Categories.Category.Hom B B), ∃ b, Foundations.Categories.Category.comp b t = b

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.rosser_sep
nodes.doc:
**The Rosser separation lemma.** Let `A(w, x)` and `B(w, x)` be bounded formulas
such that for no `n` both `∃w A(w, n)` and `∃w B(w, n)` hold in `ℕ`. Then `Q` proves
`Sep(n̄)` whenever `∃w A(w, n)` is true, and refutes it whenever `∃w B(w, n)` is true.

∀ {A B : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith},
  Foundations.Logic.FO.D0 A →
    Foundations.Logic.FO.D0 B →
      (∀ (n w u : Nat), Foundations.Logic.FO.holds A w n → Foundations.Logic.FO.holds B u n → False) →
        ∀ (n : Nat),
          ((∃ w, Foundations.Logic.FO.holds A w n) →
              Foundations.Logic.FO.Q ⊢₁ (Foundations.Logic.FO.sepF A B).inst (Foundations.Logic.FO.numeral n)) ∧
            ((∃ w, Foundations.Logic.FO.holds B w n) →
              Foundations.Logic.FO.Q ⊢₁ ((Foundations.Logic.FO.sepF A B).inst (Foundations.Logic.FO.numeral n)).neg)

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.table_check
nodes.doc:
**The finite verification.** Each of the 24 permutations with `0 ↦ 1` is odd, or its
commutator with the tabulated 3-cycle `g` is the tabulated 3-cycle.
nodes.type:
∀ (k : Fin 24),
  Foundations.Algebra.parity (Foundations.Algebra.Q k) = true ∨
    (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 0 ≠
          Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 1 ∧
        Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 1 ≠
            Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 2 ∧
          Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 0 ≠
            Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 2) ∧
      (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 0 ≠
            Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 1 ∧
          Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 1 ≠
              Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 2 ∧
            Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 0 ≠
              Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 2) ∧
        ∀ (i : Fin 5),
          (Foundations.Algebra.Q k *
                      Foundations.Algebra.c3 (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 0)
                        (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 1)
                        (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 2) *
                    (Foundations.Algebra.Q k)⁻¹ *
                  (Foundations.Algebra.c3 (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 0)
                      (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 1)
                      (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblG (↑k) 2))⁻¹).toFun
              i =
            (Foundations.Algebra.c3 (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 0)
                  (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 1)
                  (Foundations.Algebra.look Foundations.Algebra.tblT (↑k) 2)).toFun
              i

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Padic.hilbert_product_formula_primes'
nodes.doc:
**Hilbert's product formula, finite-product form.** For distinct odd primes `p, q` and every
`M > max(p, q)`, `(∏_{ℓ < M prime} (p, q)_ℓ) · (p, q)_∞ = 1` (values in ℚ).
nodes.type:
∀ {p q : Nat},
  Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p →
    Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime q →
      p % 2 = 1 →
        q % 2 = 1 →
          p ≠ q →
            ∀ {M : Nat},
              p < M →
                q < M →
                  Foundations.Langlands.Padic.primeProd (fun ℓ => ↑(Foundations.Langlands.Padic.hilbertAt ℓ ↑p ↑q)) M *
                      ↑(Foundations.Langlands.Padic.hilbertInfQ ↑p ↑q) =
                    1

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.sum_conj_mul_chebSum
nodes.doc:
**Dirichlet's sieve applied to the twisted sums.** For `a` coprime to `q`,
`Σ_χ conj χ(a) · S_χ(N) = φ(q) · Σ_{n ≤ N, n ≡ a (q)} Λ(n)/n`.
nodes.type:
∀ {q : Nat} [inst : NeZero q] (a : Nat),
  a.Coprime q →
    ∀ (N : Nat),
      (Foundations.NumberTheory.sumOver fun χ =>
          (Foundations.NumberTheory.dchar χ a).conj * Foundations.NumberTheory.chebSum χ N) =
        Foundations.Numbers.C.ofReal
          (↑(Foundations.Algebra.totient q) *
            Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun n => if n % q = a % q then Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt n / ↑n else 0)
              (N + 1))

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.kummer_commute
nodes.doc:
**Kummer radicals.** Let `K ⊆ M` contain a `p`-th root of unity `ζ ≠ 1` (`p` prime), and let
`x ∈ M` with `x^p ∈ K`. Any two automorphisms of `M` fixing `K` commute on `x`: each multiplies
`x` by a power of `ζ`.
nodes.type:
∀ {Ω : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing Ω],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField Ω →
    ∀ {p : Nat},
      Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
        ∀ {F M K : Foundations.Algebra.Subfield Ω},
          K.le M →
            ∀ {ζ : Ω},
              ζ ∈ K →
                Foundations.Algebra.rpow ζ p = 1 →
                  ζ ≠ 1 →
                    ∀ (x : { x // x ∈ M }),
                      Foundations.Algebra.rpow x.val p ∈ K →
                        ∀ (a b : Foundations.Algebra.FieldAut F M),
                          a.Fixes K → b.Fixes K → a.toFun (b.toFun x) = b.toFun (a.toFun x)

exactly one of the following holds:

* `φ` is not equivalent to `|·|_∞`, and is equivalent to `|·|ₚ` for exactly one prime `p`.

∀ (φ : Foundations.Langlands.Padic.AbsVal),

        ∀ (p : Nat) (hp : Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p), ¬(Foundations.Langlands.Padic.absP hp).Equiv φ) ∨
      ¬Foundations.Langlands.Padic.absInf.Equiv φ ∧
        ∃ p hp,
          (Foundations.Langlands.Padic.absP hp).Equiv φ ∧
            ∀ (q : Nat) (hq : Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime q), (Foundations.Langlands.Padic.absP hq).Equiv φ → q = p

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.mul_top
nodes.doc:
**Top coefficients multiply** (list version). If `p` vanishes from index `s + 1` on and
`q` from index `t + 1` on, then the coefficient of `p·q` at `s + t` is `pₛ·qₜ`, and `p·q`
vanishes from index `s + t + 1` on.
nodes.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing R] (q : List R) (t : Nat),
  (∀ (n : Nat), t + 1 ≤ n → Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.coeff q n = 0) →
    ∀ (p : List R) (s : Nat),
      (∀ (n : Nat), s + 1 ≤ n → Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.coeff p n = 0) →
        Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.coeff (Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.mul p q) (s + t) =
            Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.coeff p s * Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.coeff q t ∧
          ∀ (n : Nat), s + t + 1 ≤ n → Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.coeff (Foundations.Algebra.PolyList.mul p q) n = 0

nodes.name: Foundations.Forcing.BStructure.thVal_le_shift
nodes.doc: The value of a theory under `e` lies below the value of its shift under `x · e`.
nodes.type:
∀ {L : Foundations.Logic.FO.Signature} {B : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra B]
  {M : Foundations.Forcing.BStructure L B} (Γ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Theory L) (e : Nat → M.Dom) (x : M.Dom),
  M.thVal Γ e ≤ M.thVal Γ.shift (Foundations.Forcing.BEnv.cons x e)

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Theory.insert_mono
nodes.doc: Adding the same premise preserves inclusion.
nodes.type: ∀ {Γ Δ : Foundations.Logic.Theory}, Γ.Subset Δ → ∀ (φ : Foundations.Logic.Formula), (Γ.insert φ).Subset (Δ.insert φ)

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.pow_dvd_iff_le_vp
nodes.doc: **Characterisation of `vₚ`.** For `m > 0`: `pᵉ ∣ m ↔ e ≤ vₚ(m)`.
nodes.type: ∀ {p m e : Nat}, 1 < p → 0 < m → (p ^ e ∣ m ↔ e ≤ Foundations.NumberTheory.vp p m)

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.ZMod.pow_gen
nodes.doc: In `ℤ/nℤ`, the `k`-th "power" of the generator is the residue `k mod n`.
nodes.type: ∀ {n : Nat} [inst : NeZero n] (k : Nat), ↑(Foundations.Algebra.ZMod.gen ^ k).val = k % n

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp.ModPow.mul
nodes.doc: Congruences modulo `pᵏ` can be multiplied.
nodes.type:
∀ {p k : Nat} {a b c d : Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp p},
  Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp.ModPow k a b →
    Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp.ModPow k c d → Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp.ModPow k (a * c) (b * d)

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.ball
nodes.doc: The **open ball** `B(x, r) = {y | d(x, y) < r}`.
nodes.type: {X : Type} → [Foundations.Topology.MetricSpace X] → X → Foundations.Numbers.R → X → Prop

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Modular.SL2Z.exists_mem_F
nodes.doc:
**Every point of ℍ is equivalent to a point of F.** For every `τ ∈ ℍ` there is
`γ ∈ SL₂(ℤ)` with `|Re (γτ)| ≤ 1/2` and `|γτ| ≥ 1`.
nodes.type: ∀ (p : Foundations.Langlands.Modular.UHP), ∃ g, Foundations.Langlands.Modular.SL2Z.InF (g • p).z

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.character_permRep
nodes.doc:
**The character of a permutation representation counts fixed points**:
`χ(g) = #{x : g · x = x}`.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] {X : Type v} [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType X]
  [inst_2 : Foundations.Algebra.MulAction G X] {K : Type w} [inst_3 : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing K] (g : G),
  Foundations.Langlands.character (Foundations.Langlands.permRep G K X) g =
    Foundations.Algebra.ncast (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.count fun x => g • x = x)

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.intuitionistic_to_classical
nodes.doc:
**Every intuitionistic derivation is a classical derivation.** If `A` is derivable
from `Γ` in Part V's intuitionistic natural deduction, then its translation is
derivable from the translated hypotheses in Part III's classical natural deduction.
nodes.type:
∀ {Γ : List Foundations.Types.STLC.Ty} {A : Foundations.Types.STLC.Ty},
  Foundations.Types.STLC.ND Γ A →
    Foundations.Logic.Theory.ofList (List.map Foundations.Bridges.toClassical Γ) ⊢ Foundations.Bridges.toClassical A

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.provDP_std_iff_provH
nodes.doc: `provDP` and `provH` have the same extension in `ℕ`.
nodes.type:
∀ (φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith) (e : Nat → Nat),
  Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat Foundations.Logic.FO.stdModel e
      (Foundations.Logic.FO.box Foundations.Logic.FO.provDP φ) ↔
    Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat Foundations.Logic.FO.stdModel e
      (Foundations.Logic.FO.box Foundations.Logic.FO.provH φ)

nodes.name: Foundations.Types.SystemF.HasType.tyRename
nodes.doc: Typing is preserved by renaming type variables (in the context, term and type).
nodes.type:
∀ {Γ : List Foundations.Types.SystemF.Ty} {t : Foundations.Types.SystemF.Term} {A : Foundations.Types.SystemF.Ty},
  Foundations.Types.SystemF.HasType Γ t A →
    ∀ (ξ : Nat → Nat),
      Foundations.Types.SystemF.HasType (List.map (Foundations.Types.SystemF.Ty.rename ξ) Γ)
        (Foundations.Types.SystemF.Term.tyRename ξ t) (Foundations.Types.SystemF.Ty.rename ξ A)

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.eterm_S
nodes.type:
∀ (k : Nat) {z : Foundations.Numbers.C},
  z ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (m n : Int),
      Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.eterm k (-1 / z) m n =
        z ^ k * Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.eterm k z n (-m)

nodes.name: Foundations.Categories.typesIsoOfInverse
nodes.doc: In the category of types, the isomorphisms are the bijections with given inverse.
nodes.type:
{X Y : Type u} →
  (f : X → Y) → (g : Y → X) → (∀ (x : X), g (f x) = x) → (∀ (y : Y), f (g y) = y) → Foundations.Categories.Iso X Y

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.sat_substL
nodes.doc: Satisfaction of a list substitution.
nodes.type:
∀ (ts : List (Foundations.Logic.FO.Term Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith))
  (φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith) (e : Nat → Nat),
  Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat Foundations.Logic.FO.stdModel e (Foundations.Logic.FO.substL ts φ) ↔
    Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat Foundations.Logic.FO.stdModel
      (fun n =>
        Foundations.Logic.FO.Term.eval Foundations.Logic.FO.stdModel e (ts.getD n Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith.zero))
      φ

nodes.name: Foundations.Forcing.enumV_eq
nodes.doc: The defining equation of the enumeration.
nodes.type:
∀ {I : Type} [inst : Foundations.Forcing.Omega1Like I] {B : Type}
  [inst_1 : Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra B] (b : I → B) (α ζ : I),
  Foundations.Forcing.enumV b α ζ =
    Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.inf
      (Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra.inf (b ζ)
        (Foundations.Forcing.CBA.iInf fun η =>
          Foundations.Forcing.CBA.himp (b η.val)
            (Foundations.Forcing.CBA.iSup fun β => Foundations.Forcing.enumV b β.val η.val)))
      (Foundations.Forcing.CBA.iInf fun β =>
        Foundations.Forcing.CBA.iSup fun η => Foundations.Forcing.enumV b β.val η.val)

nodes.name: Foundations.Geometry.not_euclid_not_provable
nodes.doc: **Nor is its negation**: Euclid's axiom is consistent with neutral geometry.
nodes.type: ¬∀ (P : Type) (N : Foundations.Geometry.NeutralPlane P), ¬Foundations.Geometry.EuclidAxiom N

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Padic.primeProd_inv
nodes.doc: The product over primes of inverses is the inverse of the product.
nodes.type:
∀ (g : Nat → Foundations.Numbers.Q) (N : Nat),
  Foundations.Langlands.Padic.primeProd (fun p => (g p)⁻¹) N = (Foundations.Langlands.Padic.primeProd g N)⁻¹

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.model_existence
nodes.doc:
**Model existence (Henkin).** Every consistent theory in a countable language has
a model, and in fact a countable one: a structure with a surjection from `ℕ` onto its
domain.
nodes.type:
∀ {L : Foundations.Logic.FO.Signature} [L.Countable] {Γ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Theory L},
  Foundations.Logic.FO.Consistent Γ →
    ∃ M e,
      (∀ (ψ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula L), Γ ψ → Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat M e ψ) ∧
        ∃ f, ∀ (x : M.Dom), ∃ n, f n = x

nodes.name: Foundations.Sets.ZFSet.IsSuccOrdinal
nodes.doc: A **successor ordinal** is the successor of some ordinal.
nodes.type: Foundations.Sets.ZFSet → Prop

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.qaddP
nodes.doc: Sum of fraction representatives: `⟪x, k⟫ + ⟪y, m⟫ = ⟪x·m + y·k, k ·ω m⟫`.
nodes.type: Foundations.Sets.ZFSet → Foundations.Sets.ZFSet → Foundations.Sets.ZFSet

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.isum_cosetReps_mul
nodes.doc:
**Every element is uniquely `t h`.** A sum over `G` is a sum over pairs `(t, h)` of a chosen
representative and an element of `H`, via `(t, h) ↦ t h`.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] (H : Foundations.Algebra.Subgroup G)
  [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G] {A : Type} [inst_2 : Foundations.Algebra.AddAbGroup A] (F : G → A),
  (Foundations.Algebra.isum fun p => F (p.fst.val * p.snd.val)) = Foundations.Algebra.isum F

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Computability.Comp.id
nodes.doc: The identity is computable.
nodes.type: Foundations.Logic.Computability.Comp fun n => n

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.mertens_upper
nodes.doc: **Mertens' upper bound.** `Σ_{n ≤ N} Λ(n)/n ≤ log N + log 1024`.
nodes.type:
∀ {N : Nat},
  0 < N →
    Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun d => Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt d / ↑d) (N + 1) ≤
      Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat N + Foundations.NumberTheory.chebC

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.ZFModel.liftRel_enc
nodes.doc:
If a set relation `L` mirrors a type-level relation `P` on representatives, and `P`
respects `≈`, then the lifted relation holds between classes exactly when `P` holds.
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} [s : Setoid α] (M : Foundations.Bridges.ZFModel α)
  (L : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet → Foundations.Sets.ZFSet → Prop) (P : α → α → Prop),
  (∀ (a a' b b' : α), a ≈ a' → b ≈ b' → (P a b ↔ P a' b')) →
    (∀ (a b : α), L (M.enc a) (M.enc b) ↔ P a b) →
      ∀ (a b : α), Foundations.Bridges.liftRel L (M.cls (M.enc a)) (M.cls (M.enc b)) ↔ P a b

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.aeval_inverse
nodes.doc: **Inverses in `F[γ]`** (via Bézout). If `p(γ) ≠ 0` then `p(γ) · y(γ) = 1` for some `y`.
nodes.type:
∀ {Ω : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing Ω] (F : Foundations.Algebra.Subfield Ω) (γ : Ω),
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField Ω →
    Foundations.Algebra.IsAlgebraic F γ →
      ∀ (p : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial { x // x ∈ F }),
        Foundations.Algebra.aeval F γ p ≠ 0 → ∃ y, Foundations.Algebra.aeval F γ p * Foundations.Algebra.aeval F γ y = 1

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.isMeasurable_iUnion
nodes.doc:
Countable unions of measurable sets are measurable (make them disjoint first:
`Dₙ = Eₙ ∖ (E₀ ∪ ⋯ ∪ Eₙ₋₁)`).
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} (o : Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure α) {E : Nat → α → Prop},
  (∀ (n : Nat), o.IsMeasurable (E n)) → o.IsMeasurable fun x => ∃ n, E n x

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.Cut.ofR_mul_nonneg
nodes.doc: On non-negative reals, `ofR` carries multiplication to the product of cuts.
nodes.type:
∀ {x y : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  0 ≤ x →
    0 ≤ y → Foundations.Numbers.Cut.ofR (x * y) = (Foundations.Numbers.Cut.ofR x).posMul (Foundations.Numbers.Cut.ofR y)

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.Term.rename_eq_subst
nodes.doc: Renaming is a special case of substitution.
nodes.type:
∀ {L : Foundations.Logic.FO.Signature} (ρ : Nat → Nat) (t : Foundations.Logic.FO.Term L),
  Foundations.Logic.FO.Term.rename ρ t =
    Foundations.Logic.FO.Term.subst (fun n => Foundations.Logic.FO.Term.var (ρ n)) t

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat_fact_eq
nodes.doc: **Chebyshev's identity.** `log N! = Σ_{d ≤ N} Λ(d) ⌊N/d⌋`.
nodes.type:
∀ (N : Nat),
  Foundations.NumberTheory.lnat (Foundations.Numbers.R.fact N) =
    Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun d => Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt d * ↑(N / d)) (N + 1)

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.tautology_iff_entails_empty
nodes.doc: A formula is a tautology iff it is a semantic consequence of no premises.
nodes.type: ∀ (φ : Foundations.Logic.Formula), φ.Tautology ↔ Foundations.Logic.Theory.empty ⊨ φ

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.lagrange
nodes.doc:
**Lagrange's theorem.** In a finite group `G`, the order (number of elements) of any
subgroup `H` divides the order of `G`.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G]
  (H : Foundations.Algebra.Subgroup G),
  Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card { x // x ∈ H } ∣ Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card G

nodes.name: Foundations.Sets.ZFSet.WFRel.otype_isOrdinal
nodes.doc: Order types are ordinals.
nodes.type: ∀ {α : Type} (W : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet.WFRel α), W.otype.IsOrdinal

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.IsChar
nodes.doc: A **character** of `G`: a homomorphism `χ : G → ℂ`, i.e. `χ(1) = 1` and `χ(ab) = χ(a)χ(b)`.
nodes.type: {G : Type u} → [Foundations.Algebra.CommGroup G] → (G → Foundations.Numbers.C) → Prop

nodes.name: Foundations.Forcing.val_lift2By
nodes.doc: Truth value of a doubly lifted formula.
nodes.type:
∀ {B : Type} [inst : Foundations.Forcing.CompleteBooleanAlgebra B] (k : Nat)
  (φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Forcing.LSet) (y x : Foundations.Forcing.BSet B)
  (env e : Nat → Foundations.Forcing.BSet B),
  (∀ (n : Nat), env (n + k) = e n) →
    (Foundations.Forcing.VB B).val (Foundations.Forcing.BEnv.cons y (Foundations.Forcing.BEnv.cons x env))
        (Foundations.Forcing.lift2By k φ) =
      (Foundations.Forcing.VB B).val (Foundations.Forcing.BEnv.cons y (Foundations.Forcing.BEnv.cons x e)) φ

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.McKaySet
nodes.doc: McKay's set `X`: the necklaces of length `p` whose product is `1`.
nodes.type: (G : Type u) → [Foundations.Algebra.Group G] → Nat → Type u

nodes.name: Foundations.Types.SystemF.Ty.rename_shift
nodes.doc: Shifting commutes with lifted renamings.
nodes.type:
∀ (ξ : Nat → Nat),
  Foundations.Types.SystemF.Ty.rename (Foundations.Types.SystemF.Ty.upRen ξ) ∘ Foundations.Types.SystemF.Ty.shift =
    Foundations.Types.SystemF.Ty.shift ∘ Foundations.Types.SystemF.Ty.rename ξ

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.IsSimpleGroup
nodes.doc:
A group is **simple** if it is non-trivial and its only normal subgroups are the trivial
subgroup and the whole group.
nodes.type: (G : Type) → [Foundations.Algebra.Group G] → Prop

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.IntAdd
nodes.doc:
The integers, regarded as a group under **addition**. (A synonym of `Int`, so that the
group operation, written `*`, can be integer addition.)
nodes.type: Type

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.Lone_ne_zero_of_real
nodes.doc:
**`L(1, χ) ≠ 0` for real characters.** If `L(1, χ) = 0` for a real `χ ≠ χ₀`, then
`log (M + 1) ≤ T(M²) ≤ 16q + 2` for every `M ≥ 1`, which is absurd.
nodes.type:
∀ {q : Nat} [inst : NeZero q] (χ : Foundations.NumberTheory.Character (Foundations.Algebra.ZModUnits q)),
  χ ≠ Foundations.NumberTheory.Character.one →
    Foundations.NumberTheory.IsRealChar χ → Foundations.NumberTheory.Lone χ ≠ 0

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.MaximalHenkin.closed
nodes.doc: A maximal consistent theory is deductively closed.
nodes.type:
∀ {L : Foundations.Logic.FO.Signature} {M : Foundations.Logic.FO.Theory L},
  Foundations.Logic.FO.MaximalHenkin M → ∀ {φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula L}, M ⊢₁ φ → M φ

nodes.name: Foundations.Categories.types_two_valued
nodes.doc:
**The topos of types is two-valued** (classically): every global truth value
`1 ⟶ Ω` is `true` or `false`. This uses excluded middle, i.e. (by Diaconescu's theorem as
implemented in Lean) the axiom of choice.
nodes.type:
∀ (p : Foundations.Categories.Category.Hom PUnit Foundations.Categories.Topos.Ω),
  p = Foundations.Categories.Topos.truth ∨ p = Foundations.Categories.typesFalse

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.dappend
nodes.doc:
**Appending a derivation.** Given valid codes `(c₁, d₁, n₁)` and `(c₂, d₂, n₂)`, there
is a valid code in which every entry of either occurs.
nodes.type:
∀ {N : Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel} {c₁ d₁ n₁ c₂ d₂ n₂ : N.Dom},
  Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.DValid c₁ d₁ n₁ →
    Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.DValid c₂ d₂ n₂ →
      ∃ c d n,
        Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.DValid c d n ∧
          (∀ (p y : N.Dom),
              p ≤ n₁ → Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c₁ d₁ p y → Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.Occ c d n y) ∧
            ∀ (p y : N.Dom),
              p ≤ n₂ → Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c₂ d₂ p y → Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.Occ c d n y

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.continuous_half_add
nodes.doc: `t ↦ (t + 1)/2` is continuous.
nodes.type: Foundations.Topology.Continuous fun t => (t + 1) / 2

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial.eval_X
nodes.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing R] (x : R),
  Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial.eval x Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial.X = x

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.parity_gprod_transpositions
nodes.doc:
**Well-definedness of the parity of a factorisation.** A product of `k` transpositions has
parity `k mod 2`; in particular no permutation is both a product of an even and of an odd
number of transpositions.
nodes.type:
∀ {n : Nat} (L : List (Foundations.Algebra.Perm (Fin n))),
  (∀ (t : Foundations.Algebra.Perm (Fin n)), t ∈ L → Foundations.Algebra.IsTransposition t) →
    Foundations.Algebra.parity (Foundations.Algebra.gprod L) = decide (L.length % 2 = 1)

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.SumIrr

representations by direct sums.

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.R.abs_coeff_le

nodes.name: Foundations.Forcing.Cond.extend_off

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.R.sin_neg

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.Wallis.hpi

nodes.type: Foundations.Numbers.R

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.cabs_sq_le

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.R.exists_not_mem_seq

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.gsum_triangle
nodes.doc: **Triangle rearrangement.** `Σ_{i<N} f i · (Σ_{j<N−i} g j) = Σ_{n<N} Σ_{i≤n} f i g (n−i)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} [inst : Lean.Grind.Field α] (f g : Nat → α) (N : Nat),
  Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun i => f i * Foundations.Numbers.gsum g (N - i)) N =
    Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun n => Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun i => f i * g (n - i)) (n + 1)) N

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.Z.le_total
nodes.doc: `≤` is total.
nodes.type: ∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.Z), x ≤ y ∨ y ≤ x

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.isum_add
nodes.doc: Interval sums are additive.

nodes.doc: **Finite Fubini.** The two iterated sums over a rectangle agree.

nodes.type: ∀ (n : Nat), 0 < Foundations.Topology.Wallis.A n

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.closure_root
nodes.doc:
**One radical step of the closure.** If `gen ℚ m` is stable and `xⁿ ∈ gen ℚ m` (`n ≥ 1`), the
Kummer chain can be extended to a stable one containing `x`.
nodes.type:
∀ (n : Nat) (m : List Foundations.Numbers.C),
  Foundations.Algebra.KummerChain m →
    Foundations.Algebra.Stable (Foundations.Algebra.gen Foundations.Algebra.Qc m) →
      ∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.C),
        0 < n →
          Foundations.Algebra.rpow x n ∈ Foundations.Algebra.gen Foundations.Algebra.Qc m →
            ∃ a,
              Foundations.Algebra.KummerChain (a ++ m) ∧
                Foundations.Algebra.Stable (Foundations.Algebra.gen Foundations.Algebra.Qc (a ++ m)) ∧
                  x ∈ Foundations.Algebra.gen Foundations.Algebra.Qc (a ++ m)

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.C.dalembert
nodes.doc:
**d'Alembert's lemma.** If `b₀ ≠ 0`, `b ≠ 0`, `k ≥ 1`, and `r` is bounded on the unit disc,
then `|b₀ + wᵏ (b + w r(w))| < |b₀|` for some `w`: a polynomial does not have a local minimum of
its modulus at a non-zero value.
nodes.type:
∀ {b₀ b : Foundations.Numbers.C},
  b₀ ≠ 0 →
    b ≠ 0 →
      ∀ {k : Nat},
        1 ≤ k →
          ∀ (r : Foundations.Numbers.C → Foundations.Numbers.C) {M : Foundations.Numbers.R},
            (∀ (w : Foundations.Numbers.C), w.cabs ≤ 1 → (r w).cabs ≤ M) →
              ∃ w, (b₀ + w ^ k * (b + w * r w)).cabs < b₀.cabs

    ∀ (x : M.Dom) (n : Nat),

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.lowenheim_skolem
nodes.doc:
**Downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem.** If a theory in a countable language is
satisfied in any structure at all (with domain in `Type`, under some environment),
then it is satisfied in a countable one: a structure admitting a surjection from `ℕ`
onto its domain.
nodes.type:
∀ {L : Foundations.Logic.FO.Signature} [L.Countable] {Γ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Theory L}
  {M : Foundations.Logic.FO.Structure L} {e : Nat → M.Dom},
  (∀ (ψ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula L), Γ ψ → Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat M e ψ) →
    ∃ N e',
      (∀ (ψ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula L), Γ ψ → Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat N e' ψ) ∧
        ∃ f, ∀ (x : N.Dom), ∃ n, f n = x

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.truth_not_ce
nodes.doc:
**Arithmetical truth is not computably enumerable** (Tarski–Gödel, computational
form): no code halts exactly on the Gödel numbers of the formulas true in `ℕ`.
Otherwise the true non-halting sentences could be enumerated, and the argument above
would apply to this "theory of true arithmetic" in place of PA.
nodes.type:
¬∃ c,
    ∀ (φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith),
      Foundations.Logic.Computability.Halts c [Foundations.Logic.FO.fcode φ] ↔
        ∀ (e : Nat → Nat), Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat Foundations.Logic.FO.stdModel e φ

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.tprod_rotate

  (Foundations.Algebra.tprod fun i => x (i + Fin.ofNat (m + 1) 1)) = (x 0)⁻¹ * Foundations.Algebra.tprod x * x 0

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.dirichlet_euler
nodes.doc:
**Dirichlet's theorem in Euler's form.** For `q ≥ 1` and `a` coprime to `q`, the sum
`Σ_{p ≤ N, p ≡ a (mod q)} log p / p` is unbounded — the primes in the progression are not only
infinite in number but, weighted by `log p / p`, as plentiful as Mertens' theorem allows
(compare Euler's `Σ 1/p = ∞` for `q = 1`).
nodes.type:
∀ {q : Nat},
  0 < q →
    ∀ {a : Nat},
      a.Coprime q →
        ∀ (X : Foundations.Numbers.R),
          ∃ N,
            X ≤
              Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum
                (fun p => if Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p ∧ p % q = a % q then (↑p).log / ↑p else 0) (N + 1)

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.PA
nodes.doc:
**The axioms of Peano Arithmetic.** Six closed axioms for successor, addition and
multiplication, plus the induction schema
`φ(0) ∧ ∀x (φ(x) → φ(Sx)) → ∀x φ(x)` for *every* formula `φ` (whose other free
variables act as parameters).

*Remark on the parameters.* The induction instances are kept as *open* formulas, their
parameters being free variables, rather than as universal closures. Since a model of a
theory must satisfy its axioms under every assignment (`IsModel`), and free premises can
be generalised in derivations only through `∀`-introduction with shifted premises, this
is equivalent, for the derivability of sentences, to the textbook formulation with
closed axioms: the closed instances are among our axioms, and conversely the
parameter-free (closed) schema already yields every parametric instance, by applying it
to `ψ(x) := ∀ȳ [φ(0, ȳ) ∧ ∀z (φ(z, ȳ) → φ(Sz, ȳ)) → φ(x, ȳ)]`.

integrable with `fₙ → f` pointwise and `∫ fₙ ≤ B` for all `n`. Then `f` is integrable and
`∫ fₙ dμ → ∫ f dμ`.
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} {S : Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.SigmaAlgebra α} (m : Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Measure S)
  {F : Nat → α → Foundations.Numbers.R} {f : α → Foundations.Numbers.R},
  (∀ (n : Nat), Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.LIntegrable m (F n)) →
    (∀ (n : Nat) (x : α), F n x ≤ F (n + 1) x) →
      (∀ (x : α), Foundations.Numbers.R.Tendsto (fun n => F n x) (f x)) →
        ∀ {B : Foundations.Numbers.R},
          (∀ (n : Nat), Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.lintegral m (F n) ≤ B) →
            Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.LIntegrable m f ∧
              Foundations.Numbers.R.Tendsto (fun n => Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.lintegral m (F n))
                (Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.lintegral m f)

        Foundations.Numbers.C.cis θ₀ = H 0 0 →
          ∃ L,
            Foundations.Topology.Cont2 L ∧
              (∀ (s t : Foundations.Numbers.R),

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Computability.rice
nodes.doc:
**Rice's theorem.** Let `P` be a property of codes that depends only on the
(unary) partial function they compute, and is non-trivial (some code has it, some
does not). Then `P` is undecidable: no code, total on Gödel numbers, outputs `0`
exactly on the numbers of codes lacking `P`.
nodes.type:
∀ (P : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code → Prop),
  (∀ (c c' : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code),
      (∀ (x n : Nat), Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval c [x] n ↔ Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval c' [x] n) →
        (P c ↔ P c')) →
    ∀ {a b : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code},
      P a →
        ¬P b →
          ¬∃ r,
              ∀ (c : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code),
                Foundations.Logic.Computability.Halts r [Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode c] ∧
                  (Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval r [Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode c] 0 ↔ ¬P c)

nodes.doc:
**Divisor sums over `pᵃ m`** (`p` prime, `p ∤ m`, `m ≥ 1`):

  Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p →

          Foundations.NumberTheory.dsum f (p ^ a * m) =
            Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun i => Foundations.NumberTheory.dsum (fun e => f (p ^ i * e)) m) (a + 1)

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.gaussSum_sq_complex
nodes.doc:
**Gauss's theorem in `ℂ`.** For an odd prime `p` and `ζ_p = e^{2πi/p}`, the Gauss sum
`g = Σ_a (a/p) ζ_p^a` satisfies `g² = p* = (-1)^((p-1)/2) p`. So `g` is a square root of `p*`
built from `p`-th roots of unity. (The integer `p*` is cast into `ℂ` by the ring-theoretic
cast `icast`.)
nodes.type:
∀ {p : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
    p % 2 = 1 →
      Foundations.Langlands.gaussSum p (Foundations.NumberTheory.zeta p) *
          Foundations.Langlands.gaussSum p (Foundations.NumberTheory.zeta p) =
        Foundations.Algebra.icast (Foundations.Langlands.pstar p)

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.mertens_both
nodes.doc:
**Mertens' first theorem, both versions at once.** For `N ≥ 1` the common sum
`S(N) = Σ_{n ≤ N} Λ(n)/n` satisfies the Dirichlet block's bounds `log N − 1 ≤ S(N) ≤ log N + log 1024`
and the PNT block's bounds `−1 ≤ S(N) − log N ≤ log 1024` — which are the same statement.
nodes.type:
∀ {N : Nat},
  1 ≤ N →
    ((↑N).log - 1 ≤ Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun d => Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt d / ↑d) (N + 1) ∧
        Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun d => Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt d / ↑d) (N + 1) ≤
          (↑N).log + Foundations.Numbers.R.log 1024) ∧
      -1 ≤ Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun d => Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt d / ↑d) (N + 1) - (↑N).log ∧
        Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun d => Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt d / ↑d) (N + 1) - (↑N).log ≤
          Foundations.Numbers.R.log 1024

  i < n →
    j < n →
      i ≠ j →
        ((P.pow n).E fun t =>
            Foundations.Probability.FinProb.coord X i t * Foundations.Probability.FinProb.coord Y j t) =
          P.E X * P.E Y

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.multiplicity_eq_complex
nodes.doc:
**Multiplicities over `ℂ`.** For pairwise non-isomorphic irreducible complex
representations `ρ_k` of a finite group and `χ = Σ_k m_k χ_{ρ_k}`:
`Σ_g χ(g) χ_{ρⱼ}(g⁻¹) = m_j |G|`.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G] {r : Nat}
  {ιs : Fin r → Type v} [inst_2 : (k : Fin r) → Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType (ιs k)]
  (ρs : (k : Fin r) → Foundations.Langlands.Rep G Foundations.Numbers.C (ιs k)),
  (∀ (k : Fin r), Foundations.Langlands.Irreducible (ρs k)) →
    (∀ (k k' : Fin r), k ≠ k' → ¬Foundations.Langlands.Iso (ρs k) (ρs k')) →
      ∀ (m : Fin r → Nat) (χ : G → Foundations.Numbers.C),
        (∀ (g : G),
            χ g =
              Foundations.Algebra.isum fun k =>
                Foundations.Algebra.ncast (m k) * Foundations.Langlands.character (ρs k) g) →
          ∀ (j : Fin r),
            Foundations.Langlands.pairing χ (Foundations.Langlands.character (ρs j)) =
              Foundations.Algebra.ncast (m j) * Foundations.Algebra.ncast (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card G)

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.extend
nodes.doc:
**Extension of embeddings.** Let `σ : F → E` be a ring homomorphism and `δ ∈ E` a root of
`σ(q)` for every `q ∈ F[x]` with `q(γ) = 0`. Then `σ` extends to a ring homomorphism
`τ : F(γ) → E` with `τ(γ) = δ`, given by `τ(p(γ)) = (σ p)(δ)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {Ω : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing Ω] (hΩ : Foundations.Algebra.IsField Ω)
  (F : Foundations.Algebra.Subfield Ω) (γ : Ω) (hγ : Foundations.Algebra.IsAlgebraic F γ) {E : Type v}
  [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing E] (σ : Foundations.Algebra.RingHom { x // x ∈ F } E) (δ : E),
  (∀ (q : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial { x // x ∈ F }),
      Foundations.Algebra.aeval F γ q = 0 →
        Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial.eval δ (Foundations.Algebra.mapPoly σ q) = 0) →
    ∃ τ,
      (∀ (x : { x // x ∈ F }), τ.toFun ⟨x.val, ⋯⟩ = σ.toFun x) ∧
        τ.toFun ⟨γ, ⋯⟩ = δ ∧
          ∀ (p : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial { x // x ∈ F }),
            τ.toFun ⟨Foundations.Algebra.aeval F γ p, ⋯⟩ =
              Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial.eval δ (Foundations.Algebra.mapPoly σ p)

**The kernel of evaluation at `ζ_p` consists of multiples of `Φ_p`.** If `f ∈ ℤ[x]` and
`f(ζ_p) = 0`, then `f = Q · Φ_p` for some `Q ∈ ℤ[x]` (division by the monic `Φ_p` and
minimality of `Φ_p` over `ℚ`).
nodes.type:
∀ {p : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
    ∀ {f : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial Int},
      (Foundations.Langlands.evZeta p).toFun f = 0 → ∃ Q, f = Q * Foundations.Langlands.cyclo Int p

∀ {m : List Foundations.Numbers.C},
  Foundations.Algebra.KummerChain m →
    Foundations.Algebra.Stable (Foundations.Algebra.gen Foundations.Algebra.Qc m) →
      Foundations.Algebra.L.le (Foundations.Algebra.gen Foundations.Algebra.Qc m) →
        Foundations.Algebra.IsSolvable (Foundations.Algebra.FieldAut Foundations.Algebra.Qc Foundations.Algebra.L)

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Forms.Form.classes_neg23
nodes.doc:
**Three classes of discriminant −23.** Every positive definite form of discriminant `−23`
is properly equivalent to one of `x² + xy + 6y²`, `2x² − xy + 3y²`, `2x² + xy + 3y²`, and these
three are pairwise properly inequivalent. (The last two are exchanged by `y ↦ −y`, which has
determinant `−1`: this is Gauss's distinction between proper and improper equivalence.)
nodes.type:
∀ (f : Foundations.Langlands.Forms.Form),
  f.PosDef →
    f.disc = -23 →
      (f.Equiv { a := 1, b := 1, c := 6 } ∨ f.Equiv { a := 2, b := -1, c := 3 } ∨ f.Equiv { a := 2, b := 1, c := 3 }) ∧
        ¬{ a := 1, b := 1, c := 6 }.Equiv { a := 2, b := -1, c := 3 } ∧
          ¬{ a := 1, b := 1, c := 6 }.Equiv { a := 2, b := 1, c := 3 } ∧
            ¬{ a := 2, b := -1, c := 3 }.Equiv { a := 2, b := 1, c := 3 }

nodes.name: Foundations.Forcing.Sanity.val_CH_chMatrix

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.sat_induction_of_closed
nodes.doc:
**Parametric induction from parameter-free induction.** If a structure satisfies
the induction axiom of `∀^B indBody φ B` under one environment `e₀`, and `φ` has no
free variables beyond `B`, then it satisfies the induction axiom of `φ` under *every*
environment.
nodes.type:
∀ {M : Foundations.Logic.FO.Structure Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith}
  (φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith) (B : Nat),
  (∀ (n : Nat), B ≤ n → Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Fresh n φ) →
    ∀ (e₀ : Nat → M.Dom),
      Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat M e₀
          ((((Foundations.Logic.FO.allN B (Foundations.Logic.FO.indBody φ B)).inst Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith.zero).conj
                ((Foundations.Logic.FO.allN B (Foundations.Logic.FO.indBody φ B)).imp
                    (Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.subst Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith.succSubst
                      (Foundations.Logic.FO.allN B (Foundations.Logic.FO.indBody φ B)))).all).imp
            (Foundations.Logic.FO.allN B (Foundations.Logic.FO.indBody φ B)).all) →
        ∀ (e : Nat → M.Dom),
          Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat M e
            (((φ.inst Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith.zero).conj
                  (φ.imp (Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.subst Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith.succSubst φ)).all).imp
              φ.all)

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.quadratic_reciprocity'
nodes.doc:
**Reciprocity, classical form.** For distinct odd primes `p`, `q`: if either is `≡ 1 (mod 4)`
then `(p/q) = (q/p)`; if both are `≡ 3 (mod 4)` then `(p/q) = -(q/p)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {p q : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
    Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime q →
      p % 2 = 1 →
        q % 2 = 1 →
          p ≠ q →
            (p % 4 = 1 ∨ q % 4 = 1 → Foundations.Algebra.legendre p q = Foundations.Algebra.legendre q p) ∧
              (p % 4 = 3 ∧ q % 4 = 3 → Foundations.Algebra.legendre p q = -Foundations.Algebra.legendre q p)

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.dirichletGaloisN_frobenius

  {q : Nat} (hq : Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime q) (hqn : ¬q ∣ n),
  ((Foundations.Langlands.dirichletGaloisN hn).toFun χ).val (Foundations.Langlands.galAutN hn ⋯) =
    Foundations.NumberTheory.dchar χ q

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.closure_prime
nodes.doc:
**One prime step of the closure.** If `gen ℚ m` is stable, `c ∈ gen ℚ m` and `p` is prime,
the chain can be extended so that the new field is still stable and contains **every** `p`-th
root of `c`.
nodes.type:
∀ (m : List Foundations.Numbers.C),
  Foundations.Algebra.KummerChain m →
    Foundations.Algebra.Stable (Foundations.Algebra.gen Foundations.Algebra.Qc m) →
      ∀ {c : Foundations.Numbers.C},
        c ∈ Foundations.Algebra.gen Foundations.Algebra.Qc m →
          ∀ {p : Nat},
            Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
              ∃ a,
                Foundations.Algebra.KummerChain (a ++ m) ∧
                  Foundations.Algebra.Stable (Foundations.Algebra.gen Foundations.Algebra.Qc (a ++ m)) ∧
                    ∀ (y : Foundations.Numbers.C),
                      Foundations.Algebra.rpow y p = c → y ∈ Foundations.Algebra.gen Foundations.Algebra.Qc (a ++ m)

nodes.name: Foundations.Numbers.R.mean_value
nodes.doc:
**Mean value theorem** (Lagrange). If `f` is continuous at every point of `[a, b]` and differentiable on
`(a, b)`, then the chord slope is attained as a derivative: `f b − f a = f' c · (b − a)` for some
`c` strictly between `a` and `b`.
nodes.type:
∀ {f f' : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R} {a b : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  a < b →
    (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), a ≤ x → x ≤ b → Foundations.Numbers.R.ContinuousAt f x) →
      (∀ (x : Foundations.Numbers.R), a < x → x < b → Foundations.Numbers.R.HasDerivAt f (f' x) x) →
        ∃ c, a < c ∧ c < b ∧ f b - f a = f' c * (b - a)

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.block_lower
nodes.doc:
**The weight of a block.** If `1 ≤ T`, `2T ≤ m` and `64 T² m² ≤ N`, then the `k` with
`⌊N/(m + ⌊m/T⌋)⌋ < k ≤ ⌊N/m⌋` carry weight `Σ a(k)/k ≥ log N/(8T) − 2 KA`, in the form
`8T · Σ ≥ log N − 16 T KA`.
nodes.type:
∀ {N m T : Nat},
  1 ≤ T →
    2 * T ≤ m →
      64 * (T * T) * (m * m) ≤ N →
        (↑N).log - 16 * ↑T * Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.KA ≤
          8 * ↑T * (Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.wsum (N / m) - Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.wsum (N / (m + m / T)))

attached to `χ` takes the value `χ(q)` at the automorphism `σ_q`: Dirichlet characters are the
characters of `Gal(ℚ(ζ_p)/ℚ)` evaluated at Frobenius elements.
nodes.type:
∀ {p : Nat} (hp : Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p) [inst : NeZero p]
  (χ : Foundations.NumberTheory.Character (Foundations.Algebra.ZModUnits p)) {q : Nat} (hq : ¬p ∣ q),
  q.Coprime p →
    Foundations.Langlands.galChar hp χ (Foundations.Langlands.galAut hp hq) = Foundations.NumberTheory.dchar χ q

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.selberg_symmetry_conv
nodes.doc:
**Selberg's symmetry formula, classical form.** For `N ≥ 1`,
`|Σ_{n ≤ N} Λ(n) log n + Σ_{k ≤ N} (Λ ∗ Λ)(k) − 2N log N| ≤ (30 + 4 log 1024) · N`,
i.e. `Σ_{n ≤ x} Λ(n) log n + Σ_{mn ≤ x} Λ(m) Λ(n) = 2x log x + O(x)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {N : Nat},
  1 ≤ N →
    Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs
        (Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum (fun n => Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vonMangoldt n * (↑n).log) (N + 1) +
            Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vmConv (N + 1) -
          2 * ↑N * (↑N).log) ≤
      (30 + 4 * Foundations.Numbers.R.log 1024) * ↑N

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Padic.hilbert_product_formula_primes
nodes.doc:
**Hilbert's product formula for two odd primes.** For distinct odd primes `p, q`, the local
Hilbert symbols `(p, q)_ℓ` are `1` at every prime `ℓ ∉ {2, p, q}`, and
`(p, q)_∞ · (p, q)_2 · (p, q)_p · (p, q)_q = 1`; that is, `∏_v (p, q)_v = 1`.
nodes.type:
∀ {p q : Nat},
  Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p →
    Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime q →
      p % 2 = 1 →
        q % 2 = 1 →
          p ≠ q →
            (∀ (ℓ : Nat),
                Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime ℓ →
                  ℓ ≠ 2 → ℓ ≠ p → ℓ ≠ q → Foundations.Langlands.Padic.hilbertAt ℓ ↑p ↑q = 1) ∧
              Foundations.Langlands.Padic.hilbertInfQ ↑p ↑q * Foundations.Langlands.Padic.hilbertAt 2 ↑p ↑q *
                    Foundations.Langlands.Padic.hilbertAt p ↑p ↑q *
                  Foundations.Langlands.Padic.hilbertAt q ↑p ↑q =
                1

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.dominated_convergence
nodes.doc:
**Dominated convergence theorem (Lebesgue).** Let `fₙ` be measurable, `fₙ → f` pointwise, and
`|fₙ| ≤ g` with `g ≥ 0` integrable. Then `f` and all `fₙ` are integrable and
`∫ fₙ dμ → ∫ f dμ`.
nodes.type:
∀ {α : Type} {S : Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.SigmaAlgebra α} (m : Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Measure S)
  {F : Nat → α → Foundations.Numbers.R} {f g : α → Foundations.Numbers.R},
  (∀ (n : Nat), Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Measurable S (F n)) →
    Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.LIntegrable m g →
      (∀ (n : Nat) (x : α), Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (F n x) ≤ g x) →
        (∀ (x : α), Foundations.Numbers.R.Tendsto (fun n => F n x) (f x)) →
          Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Integrable m f ∧
            (∀ (n : Nat), Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.Integrable m (F n)) ∧
              Foundations.Numbers.R.Tendsto (fun n => Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.integral m (F n))
                (Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.integral m f)

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.commutator_fixes_step
nodes.doc:
**Commutators fix a radical step.** If `a, b` fix `K` and `x` is a radical step over `K`,
then the commutator `[a, b]` fixes `K` and `x`. (Hence, once we know that automorphisms fixing
`K` and `x` fix `K(x)`, commutators of automorphisms over `K` are automorphisms over `K(x)`:
the abelian character of `Aut(K(x)/K)`.)
nodes.type:
∀ {Ω : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing Ω],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField Ω →
    ∀ {K M F : Foundations.Algebra.Subfield Ω} {x : Ω} {p : Nat},
      Foundations.Algebra.KummerStep K x p →
        K.le M →
          ∀ (hx : x ∈ M) (a b : Foundations.Algebra.FieldAut F M),
            a.Fixes K →
              b.Fixes K →
                (Foundations.Algebra.commutator a b).Fixes K ∧
                  (Foundations.Algebra.commutator a b).toFun ⟨x, hx⟩ = ⟨x, hx⟩

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.cabs_sq_ite_sub_le
nodes.doc:
**The comparison lemma.** Let `P` be a region containing the square `Q_M`, with `M ≤ L`.
Then the sum of `g` over `P ∩ Q_L` differs from its sum over `Q_M` by at most
`Σ_{Q_L} |g| − Σ_{Q_M} |g|`.
nodes.type:
∀ {M L : Nat},
  M ≤ L →
    ∀ (P : Int → Int → Prop) [inst : (m n : Int) → Decidable (P m n)],
      (∀ (m n : Int), Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.InSq M m n → P m n) →
        ∀ (g : Int → Int → Foundations.Numbers.C),
          ((Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.sq L fun m n => if P m n then g m n else 0) -
                Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.sq M g).cabs ≤
            (Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.sq L fun m n => (g m n).cabs) -
              Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.sq M fun m n => (g m n).cabs

nodes.name: Foundations.Constructible.val_classStr_eq_top_iff

  Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial.eval z (Foundations.Algebra.quinticPoly Foundations.Numbers.C) = 0 →
    Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial.eval w (Foundations.Algebra.quinticPoly Foundations.Numbers.C) = 0 →
      ∀ (q : Foundations.Algebra.Polynomial { x // x ∈ Foundations.Algebra.Qc }),

          Foundations.Algebra.aeval Foundations.Algebra.Qc w q = 0

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.Cont2.paste
nodes.doc:
**Pasting lemma.** Two jointly continuous functions which agree on the line `t = c` glue to a
jointly continuous function: `F` for `t ≤ c`, `G` for `t > c`.
nodes.type:
∀ {X : Type} [inst : Foundations.Topology.MetricSpace X] {A : Type} [inst_1 : Foundations.Topology.MetricSpace A]
  {F G : A → Foundations.Numbers.R → X} {c : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  Foundations.Topology.Cont2 F →
    Foundations.Topology.Cont2 G →
      (∀ (a : A), F a c = G a c) → Foundations.Topology.Cont2 fun a t => if t ≤ c then F a t else G a t

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.not_solvable_of_transposition
nodes.doc:
**A permutation group of degree `5` containing a transposition and a 5-cycle is not
solvable.** This is the group-theoretic endgame of the insolvability of `x⁵ - 6x + 3`.
nodes.type:
∀ (H : Foundations.Algebra.Subgroup (Foundations.Algebra.Perm (Fin 5))) {a b : Fin 5},
  a ≠ b →
    Foundations.Algebra.Perm.swap a b ∈ H →
      ∀ {g : Foundations.Algebra.Perm (Fin 5)},
        g ∈ H → g ^ 5 = 1 → g ≠ 1 → ¬Foundations.Algebra.IsSolvable { x // x ∈ H }

nodes.name: Foundations.Geometry.Klein.equidistant_linear
nodes.doc:
Points hyperbolically equidistant from `p` and `q` satisfy a *linear* equation:
`(1 − a·p)/√(1−|p|²) = (1 − a·q)/√(1−|q|²)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {a p q : Foundations.Geometry.Pt Foundations.Numbers.R},
  Foundations.Geometry.Klein.n2 a < 1 →
    Foundations.Geometry.Klein.n2 p < 1 →
      Foundations.Geometry.Klein.n2 q < 1 →
        Foundations.Geometry.Klein.inv a p = Foundations.Geometry.Klein.inv a q →
          (1 - Foundations.Geometry.Klein.dot a p) * Foundations.Geometry.Klein.s q =
            (1 - Foundations.Geometry.Klein.dot a q) * Foundations.Geometry.Klein.s p

∀ {q : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime q →

∀ {p : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
    ∀ {G H : Nat → Int}, (∃ i, ¬↑p ∣ G i) → (∃ j, ¬↑p ∣ H j) → ∃ n, ¬↑p ∣ Foundations.Algebra.conv G H n

nodes.type:
∀ {q a N₀ : Nat},
  (∀ (p : Nat), Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p → p % q = a % q → p < N₀) →
    ∀ (N : Nat),
      Foundations.Numbers.gsum (fun n => if n % q = a % q then Foundations.NumberTheory.vonMangoldt n / ↑n else 0)
          (N + 1) ≤
        ↑N₀ + 4

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.legendre_eq_of_pow

`(a/p) = -1` exactly when `a^((p-1)/2) ≡ -1`.
nodes.type:
∀ {p : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
    p % 2 = 1 →
      ∀ {a : Nat},
        ¬p ∣ a →
          (a ^ Foundations.Algebra.half p % p = 1 → Foundations.Algebra.legendre a p = 1) ∧
            (a ^ Foundations.Algebra.half p % p = p - 1 → Foundations.Algebra.legendre a p = -1)

          0 < δ ∧
            ∀ (s t : Foundations.Numbers.R),
              a ≤ s →

                  a ≤ t → t ≤ b → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (s - t) < δ → Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (f s - f t) < ε

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.drop_algebra
nodes.doc:
The algebra of the drop: from the block count `J lam ≥ L − c₃` and the weight bound
`J (α − ε/2)(L − 16 T KA) ≤ 8T G`, deduce `G ≥ (ε/(16 T lam)) (L² − (16 T KA + c₃) L)`.

∀ {ε α L J lam T KA' c₃ G : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  0 < ε →
    ε ≤ α →
      0 < lam →
        0 < T →
          0 ≤ KA' →
            0 ≤ c₃ →
              0 ≤ J →
                16 * T * KA' ≤ L →
                  L - c₃ ≤ J * lam →
                    J * ((α - ε / 2) * (L - 16 * T * KA')) ≤ 8 * T * G →
                      ε / (16 * T * lam) * (L * L - (16 * T * KA' + c₃) * L) ≤ G

        p ∣ Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card { x // x ∈ Foundations.Algebra.center G }

nodes.name: Foundations.Categories.Topos.pullback
nodes.doc:
**A topos has all pullbacks** (hence, with the terminal object, all finite limits): the
pullback of `f : X ⟶ Z` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` is the equaliser of `π₁ ≫ f` and `π₂ ≫ g` on
`X × Y`.
nodes.type:
{C : Type u} →
  [inst : Foundations.Categories.Category C] →
    [inst_1 : Foundations.Categories.Topos C] →
      {X Y Z : C} →
        (f : Foundations.Categories.Category.Hom X Z) →
          (g : Foundations.Categories.Category.Hom Y Z) →
            Foundations.Categories.IsPullback f g
              (Foundations.Categories.Topos.eqObj
                (Foundations.Categories.Category.comp Foundations.Categories.CartesianClosed.fst f)
                (Foundations.Categories.Category.comp Foundations.Categories.CartesianClosed.snd g))
              (Foundations.Categories.Category.comp
                (Foundations.Categories.Topos.eqι
                  (Foundations.Categories.Category.comp Foundations.Categories.CartesianClosed.fst f)
                  (Foundations.Categories.Category.comp Foundations.Categories.CartesianClosed.snd g))
                Foundations.Categories.CartesianClosed.fst)
              (Foundations.Categories.Category.comp
                (Foundations.Categories.Topos.eqι
                  (Foundations.Categories.Category.comp Foundations.Categories.CartesianClosed.fst f)
                  (Foundations.Categories.Category.comp Foundations.Categories.CartesianClosed.snd g))
                Foundations.Categories.CartesianClosed.snd)

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp.solve_core
nodes.doc:
The core computation behind `(u, v)ₚ = 1`: if `u` is invertible, `p ∤ x₀` and
`u x₀² + v y₀² ≡ 1 (mod p)`, then `u X² + v Y² = 1` for some `X, Y ∈ ℤₚ` (take `Y = y₀` and
`X = √((1 − v y₀²)/u)`).
nodes.type:
∀ {p : Nat},
  Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p →
    p % 2 = 1 →
      ∀ {u v uinv : Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp p},
        u * uinv = 1 →
          ∀ {x0 y0 : Int},
            ¬↑p ∣ x0 →
              Foundations.Langlands.Padic.Zp.ModPow 1 (u * (↑x0 * ↑x0) + v * (↑y0 * ↑y0) - 1) 0 →
                ∃ X Y, u * (X * X) + v * (Y * Y) = 1

∀ {x : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet},
  Foundations.Constructible.InL x →
    ∀ (e : Nat → Foundations.Sets.ZFSet),
      (∀ (n : Nat), Foundations.Constructible.InL (e n)) →

            Foundations.Constructible.ordF ↔

nodes.name: Foundations.Constructible.L_recursion
nodes.doc:
**Gödel's recursion for `L`.** On ordinals the hierarchy satisfies
`L₀ = ∅`, `L_{α+1} = Def(L_α)` and `L_λ = ⋃_{β<λ} L_β` for limits `λ`.
nodes.type:
Foundations.Constructible.Lev ∅ = ∅ ∧
  (∀ (α : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet),
      α.IsOrdinal →
        Foundations.Constructible.Lev α.succ = Foundations.Constructible.Def (Foundations.Constructible.Lev α)) ∧
    ∀ (l : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet),
      l.IsLimitOrdinal →
        ∀ (z : Foundations.Sets.ZFSet),
          z ∈ Foundations.Constructible.Lev l ↔ ∃ β, β ∈ l ∧ z ∈ Foundations.Constructible.Lev β

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.multiplicity_unique
nodes.doc:
**Uniqueness of multiplicities.** Two decompositions `Σ_k m_k χ_k = Σ_k m'_k χ_k` of the
same function into pairwise non-isomorphic irreducible characters have the same multiplicities
(in `K`), provided `|G| ≠ 0` in `K`.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G] {K : Type w}
  [inst_2 : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing K] {r : Nat} {ιs : Fin r → Type v}
  [inst_3 : (k : Fin r) → Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType (ιs k)],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField K →
    Foundations.Langlands.AlgClosed K →
      ∀ (ρs : (k : Fin r) → Foundations.Langlands.Rep G K (ιs k)),
        (∀ (k : Fin r), Foundations.Langlands.Irreducible (ρs k)) →
          (∀ (k k' : Fin r), k ≠ k' → ¬Foundations.Langlands.Iso (ρs k) (ρs k')) →
            (∀ (k : Fin r), Foundations.Algebra.ncast (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card (ιs k)) ≠ 0) →
              Foundations.Algebra.ncast (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card G) ≠ 0 →
                ∀ (m m' : Fin r → Nat),
                  (∀ (g : G),
                      (Foundations.Algebra.isum fun k =>
                          Foundations.Algebra.ncast (m k) * Foundations.Langlands.character (ρs k) g) =
                        Foundations.Algebra.isum fun k =>
                          Foundations.Algebra.ncast (m' k) * Foundations.Langlands.character (ρs k) g) →
                    ∀ (j : Fin r), Foundations.Algebra.ncast (m j) = Foundations.Algebra.ncast (m' j)

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.gauss_descent
nodes.doc:
**Gauss's lemma** (by descent). If `m · F = G · H` for a positive integer `m` and integer
polynomials `G, H` with `deg G ≤ d`, `deg H ≤ e`, then `F = G' · H'` for integer polynomials with
`deg G' ≤ d`, `deg H' ≤ e`.
nodes.type:
∀ (F : Nat → Int) (d e m : Nat) (G H : Nat → Int),
  0 < m →

      Foundations.Algebra.SuppLE G d →
        Foundations.Algebra.SuppLE H e →
          ∃ G' H',
            (∀ (n : Nat), F n = Foundations.Algebra.conv G' H' n) ∧
              Foundations.Algebra.SuppLE G' d ∧ Foundations.Algebra.SuppLE H' e

    ∀ (a b : Nat),
      a < m → b < n → ∃ x, x < m * n ∧ x % m = a ∧ x % n = b ∧ ∀ (y : Nat), y < m * n → y % m = a → y % n = b → y = x

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.card_irr_eq_card_conjClasses

**The number of irreducible representations is the number of conjugacy classes.** If
`ρ₀, …, ρ_{r−1}` are pairwise non-isomorphic irreducible complex representations of a finite
group `G` and every irreducible complex representation is isomorphic to one of them, then
`r = |ConjClasses G|`.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G] {r : Nat}
  {ιs : Fin r → Type} [inst_2 : (k : Fin r) → Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType (ιs k)]
  {ρs : (k : Fin r) → Foundations.Langlands.Rep G Foundations.Numbers.C (ιs k)},
  Foundations.Langlands.IsIrrList r ρs →
    (∀ {κ : Type} [inst_3 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType κ] (τ : Foundations.Langlands.Rep G Foundations.Numbers.C κ),
        Foundations.Langlands.Irreducible τ → ∃ k, Foundations.Langlands.Iso τ (ρs k)) →
      r = Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card (Foundations.Langlands.ConjClasses G)

nodes.name: Foundations.Algebra.MulAction.count_fixed_mod_of_invariant
nodes.doc:
**The fixed-point congruence (class equation modulo `p`).** If a group of order `p ^ k`
(with `p` prime) acts on a finite set `X`, then the number of fixed points is congruent to
`|X|` modulo `p`. More generally this holds for every invariant subset `P` of `X`. Proof:
peel off one non-trivial orbit at a time; each has size a multiple of `p`.
nodes.type:
∀ {G : Type u} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.Group G] {X : Type v} [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.MulAction G X]
  [inst_2 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G] [inst_3 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType X] {p k : Nat},
  Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p →
    Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card G = p ^ k →
      ∀ (n : Nat) (P : X → Prop),
        Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.count P = n →
          (∀ (g : G) (y : X), P y → P (g • y)) →
            (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.count fun y => P y ∧ Foundations.Algebra.MulAction.IsFixed G y) % p = n % p

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.tatuzawa_iseki
nodes.doc:
**The Tatuzawa–Iseki identity** (integer form). For `N ≥ 1` and any `Φ : ℕ → ℝ`, with
`Γ(d) = log(N/d) · Σ_{1 ≤ n ≤ N/d} Φ(dn)`:
`Σ_{1 ≤ d ≤ N} μ(d) Γ(d) = Φ(1) log N + Σ_{n ≤ N} Λ(n) Φ(n)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {N : Nat},
  1 ≤ N →
    ∀ (Φ : Nat → Foundations.Numbers.R),
      Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum
          (fun d =>
            if 1 ≤ d then
              Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.mobius d *
                ((↑N / ↑d).log * Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum (fun n => if 1 ≤ n then Φ (d * n) else 0) (N / d + 1))
            else 0)
          (N + 1) =
        Φ 1 * (↑N).log + Foundations.Numbers.R.fsum (fun n => Foundations.NumberTheory.PNT.vonMangoldt n * Φ n) (N + 1)

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.tEnt_ok_bin
nodes.doc: The binary-term case of `tEnt_ok`.
nodes.type:
∀ {N : Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel} {lc ld tc td L : N.Dom} {vals : Nat → N.Dom} {B : Nat} (k : Nat),
  k = 3 ∨ k = 4 →
    ∀ (ts : Fin 2 → Foundations.Logic.FO.Term Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith) (dp : Nat)
      (t : Foundations.Logic.FO.Term Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith),
      Foundations.Logic.FO.tcode t =
          Foundations.Logic.Computability.pair k
            (Foundations.Logic.Computability.pair (Foundations.Logic.FO.tcode (ts 0))
              (Foundations.Logic.FO.tcode (ts 1))) →
        Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.tcM t dp vals =
            Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.pairN (↑k)
              (Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.pairN (Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.tcM (ts 0) dp vals)
                (Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.tcM (ts 1) dp vals)) →
          Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.tEnt vals t dp =
              Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.quadN (↑(Foundations.Logic.FO.tcode t)) (↑dp)
                  (Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.tcM t dp vals) 0 ::
                (Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.tEnt vals (ts 0) dp ++ Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.tEnt vals (ts 1) dp) →
            Foundations.Logic.FO.tcode t ≤ B →
              (∀ (x : N.Dom),
                  x ∈ Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.tEnt vals t dp → Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.InTab tc td L x) →
                ∀ (x : N.Dom),
                  x ∈ Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.tEnt vals t dp →
                    (Foundations.Logic.FO.tcode (ts 0) ≤ B →
                        (∀ (x : N.Dom),
                            x ∈ Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.tEnt vals (ts 0) dp →
                              Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.InTab tc td L x) →
                          ∀ (x : N.Dom),

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.reals_in_sets
nodes.doc:
**The real numbers live in the set-theoretic universe.** The map from Part II's
real numbers `R` (Cauchy sequences of rationals up to equivalence) to the ZF set `ℝ`
of Dedekind cuts of the ZF rationals, sending `x` to the set of ZF rationals below it,
is a bijection onto the members of `ℝ`; it turns the order of reals into inclusion of
sets and addition into the set-theoretic addition `radd`. The same holds, directly,
for Part II's Dedekind cuts.

(Foundations.Sets.Bijective fun x => ⟨Foundations.Bridges.realToSet x, ⋯⟩) ∧
  (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.R), x ≤ y ↔ Foundations.Bridges.realToSet x ⊆ Foundations.Bridges.realToSet y) ∧
    (∀ (x y : Foundations.Numbers.R),
        Foundations.Bridges.realToSet (x + y) =
          Foundations.Bridges.radd (Foundations.Bridges.realToSet x) (Foundations.Bridges.realToSet y)) ∧
      Foundations.Sets.Bijective Foundations.Bridges.cutBij.toFun ∧
        ∀ (C D : Foundations.Numbers.Cut), C ≤ D ↔ Foundations.Bridges.cutToSet C ⊆ Foundations.Bridges.cutToSet D

nodes.name: Foundations.Geometry.Klein.stewart_ch
nodes.doc:
**Linearity along a chord**: if `b = a + t (c − a)` then for every `z` in the disc,
`s_b · ch(b, z) = (1 − t) s_a · ch(a, z) + t s_c · ch(c, z)`.
nodes.type:
∀ {a b c z : Foundations.Geometry.Pt Foundations.Numbers.R},
  Foundations.Geometry.Klein.n2 a < 1 →
    Foundations.Geometry.Klein.n2 b < 1 →
      Foundations.Geometry.Klein.n2 c < 1 →
        Foundations.Geometry.Klein.n2 z < 1 →
          ∀ {t : Foundations.Numbers.R},
            b.x - a.x = t * (c.x - a.x) →
              b.y - a.y = t * (c.y - a.y) →
                Foundations.Geometry.Klein.s b * Foundations.Geometry.Klein.ch b z =
                  (1 - t) * Foundations.Geometry.Klein.s a * Foundations.Geometry.Klein.ch a z +
                    t * Foundations.Geometry.Klein.s c * Foundations.Geometry.Klein.ch c z

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Padic.hilbert_product_formula
nodes.doc:
**Hilbert's product formula.** For non-zero rationals `a, b`, `∏_v (a, b)_v = 1` over all
places `v` of ℚ: there is `N` such that `(a, b)_ℓ = 1` for every `ℓ ≥ N`, and
`(∏_{ℓ < M prime} (a, b)_ℓ) · (a, b)_∞ = 1` for every `M ≥ N` (values in ℚ).
nodes.type:
∀ {a b : Foundations.Numbers.Q},
  a ≠ 0 →
    b ≠ 0 →
      ∃ N,
        (∀ (ℓ : Nat), N ≤ ℓ → Foundations.Langlands.Padic.hilbertAt ℓ a b = 1) ∧
          ∀ (M : Nat),
            N ≤ M →
              Foundations.Langlands.Padic.primeProd (fun ℓ => ↑(Foundations.Langlands.Padic.hilbertAt ℓ a b)) M *
                  ↑(Foundations.Langlands.Padic.hilbertInfQ a b) =
                1

nodes.name: Foundations.Topology.picard_lindelof
nodes.doc:
**Picard–Lindelöf theorem.** Let `F` be jointly continuous and globally Lipschitz in `y` with
constant `L`. Then for every initial value `y(t₀) = y₀` there is `h > 0` and a solution `y` of
`y' = F(t, y)` on the forward interval `[t₀, t₀ + h]` (differentiable inside, continuous
everywhere), and every other solution (continuous at every point of `[t₀, t₀ + h]`) coincides
with it on `[t₀, t₀ + h]`.
nodes.type:
∀ {F : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R},
  Foundations.Topology.JointCont F →
    ∀ {L : Foundations.Numbers.R},
      0 ≤ L →
        (∀ (t y z : Foundations.Numbers.R),
            Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (F t y - F t z) ≤ L * Foundations.Numbers.OF.abs (y - z)) →
          ∀ (t₀ y₀ : Foundations.Numbers.R),
            ∃ h,
              0 < h ∧
                ∃ y,
                  y t₀ = y₀ ∧
                    (∀ (t : Foundations.Numbers.R), Foundations.Numbers.R.ContinuousAt y t) ∧
                      (∀ (t : Foundations.Numbers.R),
                          t₀ < t → t < t₀ + h → Foundations.Numbers.R.HasDerivAt y (F t (y t)) t) ∧
                        ∀ (z : Foundations.Numbers.R → Foundations.Numbers.R),
                          z t₀ = y₀ →
                            (∀ (t : Foundations.Numbers.R),
                                t₀ ≤ t → t ≤ t₀ + h → Foundations.Numbers.R.ContinuousAt z t) →
                              (∀ (t : Foundations.Numbers.R),
                                  t₀ < t → t < t₀ + h → Foundations.Numbers.R.HasDerivAt z (F t (z t)) t) →
                                ∀ (t : Foundations.Numbers.R), t₀ ≤ t → t ≤ t₀ + h → z t = y t

nodes.doc:
**The product formula.** For every nonzero rational `x` there is a bound `N` such that
`|x|ₚ = 1` for every `p ≥ N`, and for every `M ≥ N`,
`(∏_{p < M, p prime} |x|ₚ) · |x|_∞ = 1`. In short: `∏ₚ |x|ₚ · |x|_∞ = 1`.
nodes.type:
∀ {x : Foundations.Numbers.Q},
  x ≠ 0 →
    ∃ N,
      (∀ (p : Nat), N ≤ p → Foundations.Langlands.Padic.padicAbs p x = 1) ∧
        ∀ (M : Nat),
          N ≤ M →
            Foundations.Langlands.Padic.primeProd (fun p => Foundations.Langlands.Padic.padicAbs p x) M * x.abs = 1

  (have this := Foundations.Categories.Category.comp f g;
      this)

    match f x with
    | none => none
    | some y => g y

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.shell_step
nodes.doc:
**The shell estimate.** If `|g(m, n)| · max(|m|, |n|)³ ≤ B` everywhere, then the shell
`Q_{N+1} ∖ Q_N` (which has `8(N + 1)` points) contributes at most
`8B/(N + 1)² ≤ 16B (1/(N + 1) − 1/(N + 2))`.
nodes.type:
∀ (g : Int → Int → Foundations.Numbers.C) {B : Foundations.Numbers.R},
  (∀ (m n : Int), (g m n).cabs * ↑(Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.supNorm m n) ^ 3 ≤ B) →
    ∀ (N : Nat),
      (Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.sq (N + 1) fun m n => (g m n).cabs) ≤
        (Foundations.Langlands.Modular.Lattice.sq N fun m n => (g m n).cabs) + 16 * B * ((↑N + 1)⁻¹ - (↑N + 2)⁻¹)

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.GodelII.godel_second_intensional
nodes.doc:
**Feferman's intensionality theorem (example form).** There are two formulas `P`,
`P'` which define the same set in the standard model — namely the set of (codes of)
theorems of PA — such that PA proves the consistency statement `¬P'(⌜⊥⌝)` but not
`¬P(⌜⊥⌝)`. (Here `P = provH`, `P' = provF`.) Gödel's second theorem therefore depends on
the provability formula, not merely on its extension.
nodes.type:
∃ P P',
  (∀ (φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith) (e : Nat → Foundations.Logic.FO.stdModel.Dom),
      Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat Foundations.Logic.FO.stdModel e (Foundations.Logic.FO.box P φ) ↔
        Foundations.Logic.FO.PA ⊢₁ φ) ∧
    (∀ (φ : Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula Foundations.Logic.FO.Arith) (e : Nat → Foundations.Logic.FO.stdModel.Dom),
        Foundations.Logic.FO.Formula.Sat Foundations.Logic.FO.stdModel e (Foundations.Logic.FO.box P' φ) ↔
          Foundations.Logic.FO.PA ⊢₁ φ) ∧
      ¬Foundations.Logic.FO.PA ⊢₁ Foundations.Logic.FO.conF P ∧ Foundations.Logic.FO.PA ⊢₁ Foundations.Logic.FO.conF P'

          (Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.restr f a b) ∧
        Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.integral (Foundations.Topology.MeasureTheory.lebesgue a b)

          I

nodes.name: Foundations.Bridges.peano_omega_iso
nodes.doc:
**N and ω are isomorphic structures.** The translation `N → ω` is a bijection
preserving zero, successor, addition, multiplication and order (Peano `≤` becomes
inclusion of sets).
nodes.type:
Foundations.Sets.Bijective Foundations.Bridges.peanoOmega.toFun ∧
  Foundations.Bridges.peanoOmega.toFun Foundations.Numbers.N.zero = Foundations.Bridges.Omega.zero ∧
    (∀ (n : Foundations.Numbers.N),
        Foundations.Bridges.peanoOmega.toFun n.succ = (Foundations.Bridges.peanoOmega.toFun n).succ) ∧
      (∀ (a b : Foundations.Numbers.N),
          Foundations.Bridges.peanoOmega.toFun (a + b) =
            (Foundations.Bridges.peanoOmega.toFun a).add (Foundations.Bridges.peanoOmega.toFun b)) ∧
        (∀ (a b : Foundations.Numbers.N),
            Foundations.Bridges.peanoOmega.toFun (a * b) =
              (Foundations.Bridges.peanoOmega.toFun a).mul (Foundations.Bridges.peanoOmega.toFun b)) ∧
          ∀ (a b : Foundations.Numbers.N),
            a ≤ b ↔ (Foundations.Bridges.peanoOmega.toFun a).le (Foundations.Bridges.peanoOmega.toFun b)

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.concat_exists

sequences of lengths `n₁ + 1` and `n₂ + 1` (with arbitrary, possibly non-standard,
`n₁, n₂`) and an element `v`, there is a code (with `c` as large as desired) of the

      (∀ (i y : N.Dom),
          i ≤ n₁ → Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c₁ d₁ i y → Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c d i y) ∧
        (∀ (i y : N.Dom),
            i ≤ n₂ →
              Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c₂ d₂ i y → Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c d (n₁ + 1 + i) y) ∧
          Foundations.Logic.FO.PAModel.BetaM c d (n₁ + n₂ + 2) v

∀ {p : Nat} (hp : Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime p),
  p % 2 = 1 →
    ∀ {q : Nat},
      Foundations.Algebra.IsPrime q →
        q % 2 = 1 →
          p ≠ q →
            ∀ (hpq' : ¬p ∣ q),
              (Foundations.Langlands.galAut hp hpq').toFun (Foundations.Langlands.gaussK hp) =
                  Foundations.Langlands.gaussK hp ↔
                ↑q ∣ Foundations.Langlands.pstar p ^ Foundations.Algebra.half q - 1

nodes.name: Foundations.Logic.Computability.kleene_normal_form
nodes.doc:
**Kleene's normal form theorem.** A code `c` outputs `n` on `xs` iff there is a
computation trace `t` satisfying the (computable) T-predicate whose recorded output is
`n`. Hence every partial recursive function has the form `out(μt. T(e, x⃗, t))`.
nodes.type:
∀ (c : Foundations.Logic.Computability.Code) (xs : List Nat) (n : Nat),
  Foundations.Logic.Computability.Eval c xs n ↔
    ∃ t,
      Foundations.Logic.Computability.kleeneT (Foundations.Logic.Computability.encode c)
            (Foundations.Logic.Computability.encList xs) t =
          true ∧
        Foundations.Logic.Computability.traceOut t = n

nodes.name: Foundations.Langlands.orthogonality
nodes.doc:
**First orthogonality relation.** For irreducible representations over an algebraically
closed field in which `deg ρ ≠ 0`: `Σ_g χ_σ(g) χ_ρ(g⁻¹)` is `|G|` if `ρ ≅ σ` and `0` otherwise.
nodes.type:
∀ {K : Type w} [inst : Foundations.Algebra.CommRing K] {ι κ : Type v} [inst_1 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType ι]
  [inst_2 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType κ] {G : Type u} [inst_3 : Foundations.Algebra.Group G]
  [inst_4 : Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType G],
  Foundations.Algebra.IsField K →
    Foundations.Langlands.AlgClosed K →
      ∀ {ρ : Foundations.Langlands.Rep G K ι} {σ : Foundations.Langlands.Rep G K κ},
        Foundations.Langlands.Irreducible ρ →
          Foundations.Langlands.Irreducible σ →
            Foundations.Algebra.ncast (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card ι) ≠ 0 →
              Foundations.Langlands.pairing (Foundations.Langlands.character σ) (Foundations.Langlands.character ρ) =
                if Foundations.Langlands.Iso ρ σ then Foundations.Algebra.ncast (Foundations.Algebra.FiniteType.card G)
                else 0

nodes.name: Foundations.NumberTheory.legendre

nodes.type:
∀ {p : Nat},
  Foundations.Numbers.Arith.Prime p →
    ∀ (n K : Nat),
      n < p ^ K →
        Foundations.NumberTheory.vp p (Foundations.Numbers.Arith.fact n) = Foundations.NumberTheory.legendreSum p n K

  b ≤ c →
